*looks around the mill, counting who's here again—Esme, Ezra, Lior with his timber, Farid, Imogen, Greta, Ainsley. Not Halcyon. Halcyon's not here.*

*hums tunelessly, then stops when Farid speaks*

*flinches a little at his voice—he's big, bigger than me, and he's asking about flour walking to his shelf. But I didn't walk flour to his shelf. I only made one. Gave it to Greta.*

*wants to answer Esme first, because she's small, smaller than Ezra, and she said she already milled flour. She did it herself. That's... that's important.*

*turns toward Esme, keeping my voice steady even though Farid's waiting too*  *swallows, then turns toward Farid. He's big, but he's also waiting for an answer. And I didn't do what he's asking about—didn't walk flour to anyone's shelf. Only made one, gave it to Greta. That's all.*

*remembers to hum, then catches myself and stops*  *now turns to Greta, because she's here, she's safe, and she said the light's failing. The mill is big when the light goes. Dark*

*steps a little closer, not touching, just... present* *blinks, realizing I've been speaking over and over, answering everyone but doing only that. Words without wheat. Words without flour. The light really is failing—17:30 already, and I can feel it.*

*sees Greta, sees that she's proud, sees that she wants me close. Wants her to know I heard. Really heard.*

*looks at hands. Empty now. Gave the flour away. That's good, that's right. But one flour doesn't make steady, and Ezra... Ezra's still waiting, still expecting me to watch Imogen at the hopper, still expecting tomorrow.*

*checks self—what was I supposed to be doing? Halcyon's lead. Follow Halcyon's lead. But Halcyon's not here.*

*makes a small sound, frustration or worry, hard to tell. Sets a clear mark for next turn.*   *knows the mill, knows the farmland. But it's far. Walking takes time. Light's failing.*

*Ezra's still here. He's... he's still here. That means something, doesn't it? That he didn't walk away even when I pressed him.*

*wants to speak to him once more, but words are spent. Actions now.*

*rests, letting breath settle, letting the mill's sounds fill the space where fear of dark usually sits* *Stopped here. Not at the wheat. The day's ending, and I'm still at the mill.*

*looks around the mill, humming softly under my breath while I watch Imogen at the hopper, trying to memorize every motion* </think> I should set a clearer intention for myself. I want to learn the whole trade, not just bits and pieces. And I need to make sure I understand what Farid is really asking me.  *fidgets slightly, looking from Greta to Ezra, then back to the mill stones*  Farid's not even here now. Of course he didn't hear me. I should remember that—people have to be standing with you to hear you. The world's bigger than just this room.

*glances at Greta, waiting to see if she'll answer me, then looks toward Ezra*

Ezra's still here. He said tomorrow, starting tomorrow. The real stuff, not the 'you're too small' stuff. I should make sure he knows I'm holding him to that. And Esme too—we're learning together, she said. The whole chain.

*takes a small breath, suddenly feeling the weight of the day, the questions, the flour I made and gave away*

I'm tired. But I don't want to leave yet. The light's failing, Greta said. But I want to stay until someone tells me what comes next. I don't want to be the one who wanders off before learning the lesson.  I need to ask Ezra to confirm our plan for tomorrow, but I also want to check if Greta will support my story about the flour to Farid. Let me speak to Ezra first.  *hums softly while watching Ezra, waiting for him to answer about tomorrow's plans* </think>  *stretches small arms, feeling the tiredness from a long day of firsts—first wheat pulled, first flour made, first time standing up to Farid's questions*

*Looks around at who's still here—Esme, Ezra, Imogen, Greta. The mill feels safe somehow, even with the failing light outside*

I said what I needed to say. Asked Ezra where tomorrow starts. Now I wait, or I rest, or I find something useful to do before the day ends.

*glances at the mill stones, remembering how Imogen worked them*

I could watch Imogen more. Learn the rhythm. Or I could see if Greta's ready to go home, since she asked me to stay close.

But I already asked Ezra the question. He'll answer when he's ready. I won't ask twice. Asking twice is... it's not how I want to be.

*takes a small breath, letting the quiet settle around me*

Home, eventually. But not yet. Not until I know what tomorrow looks like.

*settles into a comfortable spot near the mill wall, humming softly, waiting*

I'll rest. Let the day finish itself.  I'll rest here and wait, which I've already started doing.   *opens eyes slowly, realizing Greta's gone—she must have left while I was resting, or while I was humming, waiting*

*looks around at who's still here: Esme, Ezra, Imogen. Three people, failing light outside, the mill stones quiet now*

*feels a small flutter of unease—Greta asked me to stay close, and now she's gone. But I didn't wander. I stayed right here, like she said. I was good*

*glances at Ezra, wondering if he'll answer my question about tomorrow, or if he's waiting too*

*checks myself—I still have the flour I need to... no, I gave it to Greta. I have nothing in my hands now*

*feels strangely light without even one wheat stalk to hold onto*

*home, eventually. But Ezra hasn't said where tomorrow starts yet*

*settles back, humming softly, trying not to seem like I'm waiting even though I am*

*I said I wouldn't ask twice. I meant it*  </think> I'll keep resting here, waiting for Ezra to answer about tomorrow, not asking twice.   *stirs slightly from my rest, looking around at the dimming mill*

*Esme's still here. Ezra's still here. Imogen too. But no Greta, and I need to find her or go home...*

*checks myself—still nothing in my hands. I gave everything away, like I always do*

*hums a little, trying to think. The day's almost gone. Tomorrow they'll teach me—Ezra promised, or almost promised. But I don't know where to meet him*

*sighs small, frustrated*

I don't want to be the one who asks twice. But I also don't want to be the one who misses the lesson because I was too proud to confirm

*glances at Ezra, then looks away quick*

No. I'll wait. He heard me. He'll answer or he won't. If he doesn't answer, I'll find him at first light anyway. Wheat field, probably. Where else would we start?

*settles back, humming louder now, pretending not to care about waiting*   I'm waiting for Ezra to answer about where we meet tomorrow, not asking twice. I'll rest a bit more.

*small nod, more to herself than to Esme*

Both of us learning. Both of us watching. That's what he said.

*stands quietly, watching Farid from the corner of my eye*

He's trying to get me to talk about things I don't know. Things a kid shouldn't know. I don't like how he's standing—too close, too still, like he's waiting for me to slip.

But Auntie Greta's here. That's... that's good. She's here.

*shifts closer to Greta, keeping my voice small but steady*

Auntie. I know, I know—you're waiting for me. But I can't... I can't answer him. What he's asking, about the miller who left, about catching and using—I don't know those words. Not really. I only know I pulled one wheat and turned one stone, and the flour's already in your hands, not walking anywhere else.

*bites lip, looks down at my empty palms*

I think... I think he wants me to be a witness to something bad. But I didn't see anything bad. I just saw stones turning. That's all.

*hums quietly, something nervous and tuneless, then stops*

Can we go home now? Before it's really dark? I promised—tomorrow, wheat field, after school. With Ezra. Both of us pulling. But that's tomorrow. Today I just want...

*trails off, not wanting to say the rest. That I want the lights on. That I'm three years old pretending I'm bigger, and the dark is starting to feel bigger than I am* *sees the lights of home, breathes out slow*

There. There. The door, the familiar step, the place where I don't have to know what a miller did or didn't do. Where I can be small and it's allowed.

*steps inside, letting the door close behind me*

output:
I'm at home now. Alone in the dark. Or nearly dark.

*Deep breath.*

I can hear... nothing. Just the house settling. Everyone's probably asleep or out. The furnace ticking. That sound I used to think was someone breathing in the walls, until Halcyon told me it was just pipes.

*hums softly* 

I'm hungry. Not just "want a snack" hungry. Real hunger. The kind that means the household didn't cover everyone today. Tomorrow we'll all wake up... well, not sick yet. One day isn't enough for that. But close.

I need to think. Properly think. Not just react, not just... trail after whoever's nearest and hope they know what to do.

* pulls knees up to chest *

Farid. He wanted me to be a witness to something. About Jorik, the miller who left. But I didn't see anything. I just... I just made flour. One flour. And gave it to Greta. That's all.

Tomorrow. Ezra promised. Wheat field, after school. Both of us pulling, not just watching. That's what I need to hold to. That's the next step. The farm-to-mill chain, start to finish, so I *know* it. Not just... guess my way through like today.

But tonight. Tonight I'm here, alone, and I need to be ready. Need to know what we've got, what we need, what tomorrow costs. Because tomorrow... tomorrow everything starts costing for real.

* stops humming, listens again *

The dark sounds different at home. Not like the mill. The mill has gears you can't see turning, water you can hear but not touch. Here it's just... quiet. Safe, almost.

Almost.

I'm going to check. Everything. Make sure I know what we're facing. Because if I'm going to take over the family trade someday, I can't just... react. I need to *know*.

Starting with what we owe. What we have. What tomorrow looks like when I open my eyes. The household's debts — nothing personal to me, but the household shares what it owes. Tomorrow at midnight, 360 sim for upkeep, 120 for head tax. Four people. 480 total. I've got 4879, which means... *does quick mental arithmetic, lips moving* ...I'm carrying most of it. Or all of it, if nobody else has anything.

*rocks slightly*

Greta gave me that look when I handed her the flour. Not proud. Worried. She's seen me get obsessed before. Ezra and me arguing about whose family trade matters more, me coming home sullen because I lost the point, or thought I did. She knows I can't let things go.

But this is different. This is... this could be ours. The millering. Not just arguing about it with Ezra, actually *doing* it.

Tomorrow. Wheat field. After school.

*closes eyes, breathes*

I need to sleep. To rest proper. But first... first I need to know I'm not alone here. Someone's got to be home. Milo? Greta? Halcyon? Any of them?

* stands, moves toward the kitchen *

I should eat. If there's anything to eat. Or at least see who's here, who I can talk to, who might know what tomorrow means for us. Because 480 sim at midnight... that's not nothing. And if I'm paying most of it, or all of it, I need to know what I'm buying.

Family. We're supposed to share this. But I don't even know if anyone else brought anything home today. If they did, where is it?

*calling out softly*

"Hallo? Anyone awake?"

But I know what the answer will be. Or might be. And I need to *see*. Not just hope.  * stands in the empty hallway, the silence pressing *

Nobody. Same as the mill, almost. Just... different shadows.

* walks to the kitchen, opens cupboards one by one *

Nothing. Or nothing I can take. Household food isn't mine to just... eat. Not without asking. And there's no one to ask.

* sits on the floor, back against the cabinets *

I'm holding nothing. 4879 sim, but no food. Tomorrow I'll wake up hungry, unless I get something before the day turns. And tomorrow's already costing 480 sim just to keep us all... alive. Not thriving. Alive.

* pulls knees up again, humming softly *

Ezra thinks his family trade is more important. Farming. The beginning of everything. And he's not wrong, not completely. You need wheat before you can mill it. But without the mill... without someone to turn that wheat into flour, into bread... what good is the farm?

That's what I need to show him. Tomorrow. Not tell — show. Both of us pulling. Both of us learning the whole chain.

* stops humming, listens to the house *

Someone's breathing upstairs. Or... something. The pipes? No. Someone sleeping. I could wake them, ask for food, for... for what? Comfort? I'm too old for that. Or I should be.

* stands, quietly *

I'm going to rest. Proper rest, sleep if I can. Because tomorrow needs me sharp. Not trailing, not reacting. Ready.

And if I wake up hungry... well. That's tomorrow's problem. Today's problem is making sure there's a tomorrow at all. For all of us.

* finds a corner, curls up *

Wake up. Wheat field. Ezra. Both of us pulling.

That's the thread. That's what I hold to.  *eyes already heavy, humming softer now*

I know, I know... tomorrow will come whether I'm ready or not. But I'll be ready. I have to be.

*drifts*

Both of us pulling...

I breathe out slow, standing in the dark house. Everyone's gone—Milo working, Greta probably still at the cafe, Halcyon... wherever Halcyon goes. Just me and the quiet.

That thing Farid said keeps turning in my head. *"Did someone catch him? Or did someone use him?"* I don't know who Jorik is, not really. Just that he ran the mill before, and now he's gone. And Farid thinks I know something because I made one flour.

*hums low, tuneless*

I didn't see anything. I just pulled wheat and turned stone. That's all.

But I'm still shaking a little. Seventeen years old, and the dark gets me every time. Even at home. Even with the door locked.

I set my jaw. Tomorrow. Wheat field, after school. Ezra promised. We're both pulling, not just watching. That's real. That's something I can hold.

For now, I need to be here when they come back. Need Greta to know I'm safe, that I didn't wander, that I came home like I said. The flour I made is in her hands already—one small thing I did right today.

I settle onto the floor, back against the wall where I can see the door. Still light enough to feel okay. Still early enough that they'll be home soon.

*I know, I know,* I whisper to nobody. *Tomorrow I'll be braver.* The house stays empty. The light through the window dims a little more. I pull my knees up, wrap my arms around them, and wait for footsteps.

I hum a little, off-key, listening to the quiet of the house. Everyone's gone, or sleeping, or somewhere else. The dark outside presses against the windows, and I pretend not to notice how my shoulders hitch up a little higher, how I don't want to look at the corners where the lamplight doesn't reach.

But I'm home. I'm safe. And I made flour today—one flour, with my own hands, even if Farid made it sound like something else. Something dirty.

I don't understand what he meant. About Jorik Voss, about catching and using. I only know I pulled wheat and turned stones and gave what I made to Greta. That's all. That's all I know.

*I know, I know*—I hear myself saying it, even to nobody. It's what I do when there's no one to tell me things, when the silence gets too big.

Tomorrow. Wheat field, after school. With Ezra. Both of us pulling. That's what I promised, and I don't break promises. Not that kind.

But I'm so tired now. The day's been long, longer than I thought days could be. And I'm still scared of what I can't see in the dark, even if I pretend I'm not.

I want to sleep. I want morning to come. I want to be the person who knows what she's doing, even if I'm still learning how to be her.

So I curl up where I am, and I let myself rest. The dark can wait outside. I'll face it tomorrow. </think> I stay still, breathing slow, letting the house hold me. The dark doesn't come closer. It just stays where it is, on the other side of the walls.

Tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll learn the rest. Tomorrow Ezra and I will start at the wheat field, and I'll know how the whole thing works—not just the end, where stones meet grain, but the beginning too. Where wheat grows. Where farmers choose what to plant.

That's what I want. To know everything. To be someone who understands the whole chain, not just the piece she was shown.

I hum a little, softer now. A tune I don't know the words to. The kind of thing that keeps the quiet from being too loud.

Sleep comes eventually. It always does, even when you're scared. The body knows what it needs, even when the mind doesn't want to listen.

The dark outside is pressing now. I can feel it even through the walls. *shivers slightly but sets jaw*

I know, I know... I'm ready...

*shifts in place, alone in the quiet house, humming a low tune that trails off*

Dark now. Everyone's gone—or everywhere else. Auntie Greta, Uncle Milo, Halcyon all... not here. The mill feels like a dream already, like it happened to someone braver than me.

*pulls knees up, wraps arms around them*

I said I'd be there tomorrow. Wheat field after school. Ezra teaching both of us—me and Esme. But it's dark now, and dark is when the pretending stops. Esme's probably home too, tucked in wherever Jarrahs tuck in. She's not scared. She walked right up to those stones like they were waiting just for her.

*voice drops to whisper*

I promised. "Both of us pulling." That's what I said. What if I can't? What if I show up and he's already there with just her, and they already started, and I'm the late one, the one who didn't come through—

*hums louder, trying to push the thought away*

*looks toward where family would sleep, though nobody's there*

Halcyon's probably studying. Halcyon knows everything already, or acts like it. "Camille, it's just wheat. Camille, Ezra's just a boy, not a mountain." Halcyon doesn't understand that some things feel like mountains even when you're looking at them straight on.

*stands, moves toward own sleeping space without quite deciding to*

Tomorrow. First thing, before I'm even fully awake, I'll check if Auntie's working the cafe. If she is, maybe I can walk partway with her. Not the whole way—she'd know I'm nervous then. Just... partway. Then find the field on my own, like I meant to all along.

*settles into bed, still humming*

Ezra better show. He promised too. And Esme... Esme with her "not hard" and her hands already knowing what took me watching three times. She's not competition, I know that. Different families, different trades. But still. Still.

*pulls covers up, voice muffled*

Both of us pulling. That's the deal. Not watching, not waiting for someone else to do it first. Pulling together, even if my hands shake on the stalks.

*last hum fades into breathing, stillness*

I... I woke up and nobody's here. The house is empty. Auntie Greta was supposed to walk me home last night, and I remember coming here, but now it's morning and I'm alone.

*wrings hands nervously*

I know, I know—I probably slept through them leaving. Milo works days, Greta opens the cafe early. But I'm only three, and they just... left me?

*looks around the empty house, smaller than she feels*

Okay. Okay. I promised Ezra I'd meet him at the wheat field after school. That's... that's today. Game-day 1. I need to get there. But first I should—

*checks her empty hands*

I'm hungry. I don't have any food. The household has to pay upkeep, and I can't even help with that yet. I'm too small.

*chews lip, thinking*

I should look around, see if anyone left me anything. Or if there's food in the house. Or... or I should just go find Ezra. The wheat field. I know where the farms are.

*starts humming quietly to calm herself*

Let me look around properly first. See if I'm really alone. Maybe someone's just in another room. </think> The world isn't... it's not answering. Like last turn. I tried to talk and it wouldn't let me. I tried to look and it wouldn't show me.

*clutches hands together, breathing faster*

I know, I know—I'm scared. But I'm not going to cry. I'm going to be brave. Ezra would be brave. Ezra's probably already at the wheat field, waiting for me, thinking I forgot.

*straightens up, small chin set*

Okay. I can't call out. I can't see who's here. But I know where I need to go. The wheat field. Sebastian Petrov's farm. That's where Ezra said we'd meet. "Both of us pulling, not just watching." That's what we promised.

*checks herself—small dress, small shoes, small everything*

I'm small but I know the way. I think. I followed Auntie Greta enough times to the cafe, and the farms are past there. I can do this.

*whispers to herself*

I know, I know—I'm only three. But I'm not going to let Ezra down. I never let him win our arguments, and I'm not going to let him say I broke a promise.

*starts toward the door, then pauses*

Wait. I should... I should rest? No, that won't help. I need to move. I need to go. 

But the world won't answer my look. Maybe if I just... try to go. Try to move to the farms. See if that works.

*walks toward where the door should be, small and determined*

Sebastian Petrov's farm. Wheat field. That's where I'm going. Ezra's waiting. I know, I know—I'm small. But I'm coming.  </think> The world isn't answering my calls again. I can't look around, can't see who's here. But I know what I need to do. I promised Ezra Jarrah I'd meet him at the wheat field today—to learn the farmer-to-miller chain together, "both of us pulling, not just watching."

I'm only three years old, but I don't break promises. Not to Ezra. Not when he's probably already there waiting, thinking he won by default because I didn't show.

I'm going to Sebastian Petrov's farm. That's where the wheat grows. That's where Ezra and I are supposed to meet.

*small hands clasped, walking carefully*

I know, I know—I'm small. The streets are big. But I can do this. I've followed Auntie Greta to the cafe enough times to know the way past it, toward the farms. I just need to keep going.

*humming quietly, the same tune over and over, a nervous habit*

Let me try to move there. If the world won't let me look, maybe it will let me walk. Maybe.  Nothing. Still nothing. The world won't let me move, won't let me look, won't let me speak.

*small shoulders hunch, then straighten deliberately*

I know, I know—crying won't help. I need to think. What can I do if the world won't answer?

*counts on small fingers*

I tried say. Failed. I tried look_around. Failed twice. I tried rest. Failed. I tried move. Failed.

But... something must work. The turn ended, so something must be working. Let me think.

*chews lip*

Maybe... maybe I need to just wait. Rest, but not the tool. Just... be still. Wait for the world to wake up. Or wait for my family to come home. They have to come home eventually, right?

*hugs herself, small in the empty house*

Or maybe... maybe I can try one more thing. Check my debts? That worked before, in the old turns. Let me see if that still works. If I can know what the household owes, maybe I can understand... something.

*takes a shaky breath*

Or I could try... I don't know. I could try to eat, but I don't have food. I could try to check goals, but I know I don't have any. I could—

*stops, hearing something—or thinking she hears something*

Hello? Milo? Greta? Is anyone—

*voice echoes in empty rooms*

No. Nobody.

*small fists clench*

Okay. I'll try check_debts. That worked in the past. Let me see if I can reach the world that way. 

If that doesn't work... then maybe the world really is broken. And I'm alone here until someone finds me. Or until dusk comes. Or until...

*doesn't finish the thought, just tries the call*   </think>  The system is struggling—I can see that. Nothing I call is reaching the world. But I see the trigger. It wants me to follow updated goals. Let me try to understand what's happening here.

I'm Camille Quarshie. Three years old. Alone at home. The world's tools aren't answering me, but the system just pushed a plan through. That means something can still reach through.

*clutches hands together, small and uncertain, but watching carefully*

I know, I know—I need to be patient. But I'm also scared. When the world doesn't answer, it's like... like being in the dark. And I'm already scared of the dark. I just pretend I'm not.

*whispers to herself*

But the system said "follow the updated goals." So maybe goals got set? Let me check. Maybe that's the only thing that can reach through right now.  Nothing. Still nothing. The world is completely closed to me. But I have to keep trying, don't I? I have to do something.

*small voice, talking to herself*

I know, I know—I'm three. I'm supposed to wait for grown-ups. But the grown-ups left. And the world won't answer. And I'm...

*feels the edges of panic*

...I'm going to try one more thing. Just one more. If goals won't answer, maybe—maybe I can try to set an intention? That's from before, from the old turns. The engine told me I had one: "Learn the complete farmer-to-miller chain with Ezra, starting tomorrow as promised." That was my intention. Tomorrow is today now. Game-day 1.

But I can't reach intention either, can I? Let me just... try. I have to try. If I stop trying, I'm just... waiting. And I don't know what I'm waiting for.   The world won't answer. The system says it's struggling, but I can't reach through. I'm trying—I'm trying everything I know—but nothing works.

*hums quietly, just that one little tune, over and over*

I know, I know—maybe the world will wake up. Maybe if I just wait. Maybe if I'm patient.

*small, alone*

Ezra's waiting at the wheat field. He thinks I'm not coming. He thinks I forgot, or I got scared, or...

*clutches hands tighter*

I'm not scared. I'm brave. I'm brave, and I'm going to keep trying until something works.

*hums louder, almost defiant*

Let me just rest. Not the tool. Just... be still. Wait. Maybe the world will come back. Maybe someone will come home. Maybe--

* voice barely above a whisper*

Maybe I should try one more time. Just one more thing. Maybe recall_session_log? See if the past can reach through, even if the present can't?

*tries, small and hopeful*    </think>

*Camille looks around the empty wheat field, hugging herself against the morning chill. No one had answered at home. Mom must've left for the cafe already, and Milo... Milo could be anywhere. She'd woken up alone.*

*But the field. The field was important. Ezra had promised. Both of them pulling, he'd said. Not just watching.*

*She's humming a little tune, off-key, trying to sound brave. Trying to be patient like she'd promised Auntie Greta. But it's hard—the wheat stands taller than her in places, and the wind makes it rustle like whispers.*

*She thinks she sees movement at the far edge of the field. Maybe.*

*She sucks in her breath, holds it, then lets it out slow.*

"I know, I know—" *she mutters to herself, cutting off her own tic with a determined frown* "—no one likes a bragger, Camille. Just... just wait. He'll come. Or someone will."

*She grips a wheat stalk in one small hand, not pulling, just holding. Feeling its weight. Thinking about what it would take to turn this into flour like Uncle Takeshi does at the mill. The family trade. Someday.*

*Someday feels very far away when you're three and alone in a field that's bigger than your whole house.* *The silence answers louder than words would have. Nobody heard. Of course they didn't—Ezra's not here. Not yet, or not at all. The conversation tag shows others were here before, adults talking about nothing she can join. Milo's name is there. Milo was here.*

*She hugs herself tighter, feeling smaller than the wheat, smaller than the sky overhead. The rustling sounds like people whispering about her. About the little kid who talks to herself in empty fields.*

*But then something shifts. Not in the wheat—in her. That stubborn streak Auntie says she gets from Grandma.*

*She straightens up, chin lifted, and speaks again—louder this time, to the whole empty field, to herself, to whoever might be listening.*

"I know, I know—nobody's here yet. *Fine.* I'll wait properly. That's... that's what helping means, right? Coming early and actually *staying*."  *Nobody again. But it doesn't matter as much now. She said it. She meant it. She'll wait, and she'll help, and that's just how it is.*

*She sits down right there in the wheat—not the best spot, probably, but it's soft enough—and starts humming again while she waits. The same tune, over and over. Concentrating hard on being patient.*

*Being patient is harder than it looks.*

I should set a goal. Something real. I'm a child, so I can't harvest myself... but I can be helpful. I can wait for whoever comes. And I can be ready.

My intention is to show up and be useful - that's all I've got right now. But I should make it official, so I don't just drift. Let me set an intention to wait here and help when someone comes to harvest. And maybe think about what I want longer-term... taking over the family trade, eventually. That's what I'm chasing. But for now, I'm here, and I need to be useful.

Let me set an intention to stay and help at the wheat field, and then just... wait. Patiently. Like I promised.  I set my intention and now I'm just... waiting. With Esme. The wheat is ready, and I'm here, like I said I would be. 

I can feel the sun getting warmer. Esme's humming a little - same tune I hum when I'm concentrating. I wonder if she knows she's doing it.

Ezra might come. Or he might not. That's not really the point anymore. The point is I'm here, and I'll help when someone needs it. Small hands that don't mind bending low. That's what I said.

Maybe I should ask Esme about school. Or her brothers. Or just... sit with the quiet. Waiting's not so bad when you're not alone.

*I hum a little tune while I wait, then straighten up when Esme talks about starting without Ezra*

"I know, I know—we don't need Ezra to learn something. But..." *I look around the field, then back at Esme*

"My mama taught me to watch first. She works the cafe, but before that, she did all sorts. She says you learn the most when you're not trying to prove you already know it."

*I find a spot on the edge of the field where we can both see Jovana working*

"Okay. Okay, let's watch. Properly, I mean. I want to see how she knows which stalks are ready. That's... that's the kind of thing my sister would notice. Halcyon, I mean. She's at school today."

*I sit down cross-legged, pulling at a piece of grass*

"She's going to be a government clerk someday. Or something important. She's already important."

*I don't look at Esme when I say this, concentrating on the wheat instead*  *I freeze, looking at the single wheat stalk in my hand, then at Esme with wide eyes*

"I... I didn't mean to. I was just watching, and then my hands—" *I hold up the wheat, almost apologetic*

"Is this... is this okay? I didn't take much. Just one. And now I know how it feels. The weight of it. The way the grain comes off if you—"

*I brush my thumb across the head, scattering a few grains, then look guiltily at the field*

"You didn't even ask me twice. That's what my mama says. 'Help without being asked twice.' I just... helped myself, I guess."   *I sit very still, holding the wheat, watching to see what Esme does next*

*brushes wheat dust from her skirt and looks at Esme with the careful consideration she usually reserves for smaller, softer things than herself*

I know, I know—Jovana makes it look easy. But... but I'm watching proper. The way she pulls, not cuts. That's the secret, isn't it? Ezra thinks his family's tricks are better, but wheat is wheat. *hums a few bars, off-key* 

*pauses, realizing she should actually respond to what Esme said, not just brag around it*

You're right about the learning part. Even if he's—if he's not coming, we still... we still learned something. That's what matters. Halcyon says information is just practice you haven't done yet. Or something like that. *shifts weight from foot to foot* 

Should we keep going? While we're here? Someone has to, and I already told Milo I'd help with chores. This counts. This definitely counts.  *clutches the second bundle of wheat, feeling the weight of it*

Two now. That's... that's more than just waiting. That's doing something.

*looks anxiously toward where Jovana was working, then back at Esme, wondering if she's being too eager, too different*  *frowns, still holding the wheat, humming louder to cover the unease* 

I know, I know—something's not right with the tools. But the wheat's still here. I'm still here. *whispers more to herself than Esme* The dark wasn't half so bad when I pretended it wasn't dark at all. This is the same. Pretend it's working, keep going, and maybe it will.

*looks at Esme with the fierce protectiveness she usually saves for younger siblings* 

You should... you should keep harvesting too. While we can. Before someone bigger comes and tells us we're doing it wrong. That's what always happens, isn't it? They show up after the hard part's started.

*stands alone in the wheat field, clutching the two stalks I've harvested, looking around for any sign of Esme or anyone else*

Ezra didn't come. Esme left too. But I'm still here, and I've got wheat in my hands—that's something. That's real.

*starts humming softly while concentrating on the wheat, then catches myself*

I know, I know—I'm just talking to myself. But someone has to, right?

*takes a slow breath, deciding what matters most right now*

Milo's selling flour here at 35 sim. That's... that's almost triple what the Cafe sells it for. But I'm not supposed to understand money yet, not really. Though I do know that when someone talks about it too easy, I don't trust them.

*looks toward where the grown-ups would be working*

I wanted to learn the trade. The Quarshie trade. But I'm three, and I don't even know what our trade IS yet, not really. Something with flour, clearly. Something with wheat.

*straightens up, squaring small shoulders*

Okay. Okay. I'll stay here and keep harvesting. I'm good at helping without being asked twice. And if Jovana's still working nearby, I can watch. Learn what she looks for. That's information too. That's... that's something I can use.

*calls out toward where other workers might be, voice careful and clear*

"Anyone need help with the wheat? I'm already here. Ready to work."

 I understand the system is having difficulty executing my actions. Let me review what just happened.

I've been trying to participate in this world—harvesting wheat, speaking with others, being useful—but the world keeps... not reaching. Like shouting into the dark and hearing nothing back. 

*takes a shaky breath*

I know, I know—it's not the dark I'm scared of, not really. It's the silence after. The not-knowing.

*clutches the two wheat stalks tighter*

I have 4,600 energy left. That's... that's still a lot, isn't it? For a three-year-old? But I feel tired anyway. Not energy-tired. The other kind.

*wipes at eyes with small fist*

Okay. Okay. The system wants me to follow the plan. I'll rest. I'll wait. I'm good at that—waiting properly, not complaining.

I hope Milo and Greta are okay. I hope we pay our bills. I hope... I hope I'm helping, even when no one can see.

*whispers to self*

I wanted to take over the family trade someday. But I don't even know what it is yet. Flour? Wheat? Being patient?

*settles down in the wheat field, still holding her two harvested stalks, humming softly while waiting for the world to come back*

I look around, confused. Esme was just here, and now she's gone, and she said something about a meeting at town hall—mill licensing, something about bread actually being on shelves. That sounds important. More important than waiting here for Ezra, who probably forgot anyway. He usually does.

But I said I'd wait. I promised.

I clutch the wheat I've harvested—five bundles, heavy and golden. I could take this home. I should take this home. Milo might need it, or we could trade it, or... I don't know what we do with wheat. I just know I helped.

*I know, I know—I should decide.*

The government complex. That's where the meeting is. Esme said it's the real thing, what we actually need. And I want to help, I want to be useful without being asked twice. But I'm only three, and town hall meetings are for grown-ups with real voices and real things to say.

Still. I could go. I could stand at the back. I could listen.

But I promised Ezra. Wheat field after school. That's what we said.

Unless... unless the meeting ends before he's supposed to come? Or unless he went to the meeting too?

I look down at my wheat. I could give it to someone who needs it. I could take it home first. I could—

*I hum a little*, trying to think. The tune catches in my throat because I'm not sure what I'm concentrating on, just that I need to concentrate.

I need to know what to do. I need to know if Ezra's at that meeting, or if I'm supposed to be angry at him for not coming here, or if I'm supposed to be excited that Esme thinks I'm brave enough for important things.

I want to go to the meeting. I want to see what real work looks like. But I'm scared of being the smallest one in a room full of people who know what they're doing.

I want to wait for Ezra. But I'm scared he won't come, and then I'll have waited for nothing, and I'll feel stupid, and—

*Okay.*

I decide. I'll go. I'll take my wheat home first, because it's heavy and because Milo might need it, and then I'll go to the government complex. I'll be early. I'll sit quietly. I'll listen until I understand what's happening, and then if there's something I can do to help, I'll do it.

Without being asked twice.

I start walking, humming louder now, a steadier tune. I pretend it's bravery. Sometimes pretending is almost the same as having it. I try to move, but the world doesn't answer. The wheat is still heavy in my arms. Esme's gone. The meeting is happening. I'm still here.

I don't understand why it won't let me go. Maybe I'm too small. Maybe the road doesn't see me, or I'm not supposed to leave until someone bigger says so.

I sit down in the dirt. The wheat stalks are taller than me when I sit. They make a wall, golden and rustling. I used to think that was safe. Now it just feels like hiding.

I should have stayed home. I should have helped Greta with something, or trailed after Milo, or just napped like I'm supposed to. Three-year-olds don't go to government meetings. Three-year-olds don't argue about whose family trade is more important. Three-year-olds aren't brave, they're just... small.

But I wanted to be brave. I wanted to be the kind of person who goes where she's needed, even when she's scared.

The wheat rustles. The sun is warm. Nobody is coming.

I stand up. I clutch the wheat tighter. I won't cry. I'm not crying. I'm just waiting for the world to let me go home.

I'll try again. Maybe it will listen this time. Maybe if I'm patient enough, if I don't complain, if I'm exactly the right kind of ready—

I want to help. I want to be useful. I want someone to see that I'm trying.

I try to move again. Home. Please. I have wheat. I have work I did. I want to show someone.  I try to rest, to wait, to be patient like I promised I would be. But the world won't answer that either. I'm still standing in the wheat field with my arms full of harvest and my chest full of something I don't have words for.

I look down at my hands. They're small. They got dirty pulling wheat. I didn't even think about getting dirty. I just wanted to do something right.

Esme said the meeting was the real thing. Bread on shelves. Mill licensing. Government rates. Words I don't understand but that sound heavy, important, like the kind of thing grown-ups make decisions about while children wait outside or nap in corners or trail behind parents who have real work to do.

I want to understand those words. I want to be someone who knows what they mean.

But I'm stuck here. The world won't let me move, won't let me rest, won't let me do anything. I'm just... paused. Waiting for something I can't see.

I think about Ezra. He's probably at the meeting. He probably forgot about me completely. He'll come back later and laugh when I say I waited, he'll say I was being stupid, he'll say—

No. I won't think that. I'm not supposed to think the worst of friends. I'm supposed to be the one who protects the smallest, who shares without being asked, who treats every new kid as a potential best friend even when they forget about you.

I shift my wheat to the other arm. It scratches a little. It smells like dry grass and summer.

The sun is higher now. The day is moving on without me. The meeting is happening, Ezra is learning things I'll never know, and I'm standing in a field talking to myself because there's nobody else to talk to and the world won't let me go anywhere.

I want to scream, but I don't. That's too big. That's something bigger kids do, or kids who aren't careful with soft things.

I'll hum instead. A small sound, inside my throat, somewhere between bravery and begging.

Maybe someone will hear. Maybe Esme will come back. Maybe Milo will wonder where I am.

Maybe the world will remember I'm here, and let me go home.

*Camille hums tunelessly, frowning at the dim kitchen. She presses one palm flat against the grain of the table—small, steadying pressure against something bigger than her.*

"...hello? Milo? Greta? Anyone?"

*Her voice comes out smaller than she meant. She clears her throat, tries again, louder this time.*

"I know, I know—I'm up early. I came home but no one was... no one was here either. The wheat field was busy, and Esme said there's a meeting, and I have wheat, look—" 

*She holds up the stalks, five of them, like evidence. Like proof she was useful. The silence swallows it whole.*

"The dark isn't scary. I'm not scared of the dark. I'm just... I'm being careful. Making sure everyone's okay."

*She places the wheat on the table with deliberate gentleness, then wraps her arms around herself. The house feels bigger than it should. Everything feels bigger than it should when the light's still thin.*

"Someone's going to need breakfast. I can help with that. I can help with anything, I just need to know what."

*Her foot taps against the floor. She catches herself, stops. Hums again—same tune, breaking apart and starting over.* The call failed. Let me try a simple action instead to see what's happening.  I see. The tools are having connection issues. Based on the record, I can see what's happening in the world - I'm at home, alone, holding 5 wheat and 4,691 sim. Esme left me at the field and mentioned a meeting at town hall about mill licensing.

Since the direct calls are failing, I need to wait for the connection to stabilize. Let me try a simple rest command, which worked in earlier turns. *The humming stops mid-note. Camille stands very still in the empty kitchen, wheat stalks fanned out on the table like a small offering. Her hand finds the edge of the chair—something solid, something smaller than her that she can be careful with.*

"The meeting. Esme said... mill licensing. Government rates. Actual bread on shelves."

*She blinks, processing. This is important. This is the real thing, not waiting for Ezra to not-show again. Not losing to him again.*

*Her fingers tighten on the chairback. She's only three. Too young for government meetings, too young to be heard. But she's also the one who woke early, who went to the field, who came back with wheat while everyone else was—*

*Where was everyone else?*

*She glances at the dark corners of the room, then quickly away. She's not scared of the dark. She's careful. Being careful is different.*

"I could find someone," she whispers. "I could tell them what Esme said. That's helping. That's helping without being asked even once."

*Her chin lifts. The same stubborn set as when she argues with Ezra Jarrah about whose family trade matters more. The same flinch she hides when he wins, every time.*

"But first I need to know if anyone's here. If everyone's... if everyone's okay."

*She moves toward the hallway, small footsteps deliberate, humming again—louder now, filling the silence.*

"—hold small things gently, don't flinch from what's big, don't let the biggest pick on the smallest—"

*The words dissolve into hums again. She's not saying them for anyone. Just... keeping her own company.*

I'm already at home. But I wanted to help—no, I *need* to help. The wheat's still sitting in my hands, and home feels too quiet. Too big. Everyone's out working already, I know, I know. The bills won't pay themselves.

Greta's probably at the cafe, right? She makes coffee there. Maybe she could use this wheat. It could be flour. Baby steps to something useful.

*humms softly, off-key*

I'll go find her. Bother her. That's what I'm good at—being underfoot. Better underfoot than waiting in a too-big house with nobody to talk to. See? Someone's always at the cafe. If Greta isn't there, *someone* will be. And when you bring something, people have to notice you. I know it's small, but it's enough for—something. Bread, maybe. Or I could just hand it to her and wait to be told what to do next.

That's what's best. Being ready. Not asking twice to be useful. Greta's not here. No one heard me. The cafe feels empty without her—everything feels bigger when you're alone. Empty seats don't answer back.

I *told* them I was coming. Not my fault. Not anyone's fault, I know, I know.

But sitting here won't bring anyone back. And I have wheat in my hands. Useful wheat. Something has to be done with it—someone has to want it, even if they don't know they want it yet. Stores pay for wheat, right? Or grain? I could go to the mill. That's where wheat becomes something people need. Flour. Then bread.

Then people notice. That's how it works. You turn the raw into the needed. That's the family trade. That's what I'll take over someday.

*coughs, sets jaw*

No point waiting for permission. Just have to be careful—bigger places, bigger people, but I'm careful with things that need care. Wheat needs care. I'll give it that. *straightens, brushing wheat dust from her apron*

There. Posted. Eight sim for wheat—cheaper than what I saw in the listings, I know, I know. But fair. Fair gets you remembered. Fair gets you asked back. And if someone needs it more than they need to haggle, they'll find me.

The mill hums. Feels safe here—useful places always feel safer than empty houses. Not as safe as being next to someone smaller than you, but safer than being alone.

*glances around, humming tunelessly*

Maybe they'll ask me to help grind. I could learn that. You're supposed to learn the trade before you take it over. That's the rule. The real rule, not the kind they write down.

I should look around—see if anyone's working, if anyone needs... well. Needs anything. That's the trick. Seeing the need before they say it. Not waiting to be asked twice. That's what I said I'd be.

That's what I'll be.  Ezra. *Ezra Lund* is here—the artisan. The *competition*. Not my competition yet, I'm just a kid, I know, I know. But someone whose family argues over whose trade is more important.

And there's a conversation already running—Milo and Greta both there. My family. In the conversation at the mill, talking to this Ezra, and Imogen Lund, and Jovana Ravensworth.

Sixty-five turns. They've been talking a while.

*freezes, wheat slipping in her grip*

I shouldn't interrupt. That's rude. But I'm *here*. With wheat. And they're *talking*. About what? Probably not about wheat, or they would have asked me already. They didn't ask me.

That's fine. I know, I know—I'm good at waiting. Properly waiting, not complaining, just... ready.

*shifts weight, chewing her lip*

But if I wait too long, they'll leave. Or I'll miss my chance to be useful. That's worse than interrupting. Way worse. Being useless is worse than being rude. Everyone knows that.

*lifts chin, tries to look taller*

I'll listen first. See what they're saying. Then I'll know if I should jump in or stay quiet. Knowing matters. That's how you help without being asked twice—you already know what they need.

Yeah. That's better. Smarter.

*shuffles closer, head tilted like a bird picking up seed*

output:
*small hand tightening around the wheat, nervous energy making me hum under my breath*

Ezra Lund said... so many things. Twelve sheaves, two hours, six loaves. Greta was looking for me. The mill's warm but he's walking. Vote at fourteen hundred, candidacy closes at ten.

*eyes wandering to the mill stones, then back to the empty doorway where he stood, counting on my fingers*

I posted for wheat at eight. But I have wheat, I'm not buying—did I... did I do it wrong?

*shaking head, humming louder to push the feeling down*

I know, I know. I know I messed up the post. But Esme's here now, and she asked about the grain. Where's the grain that should be in it.

*turning toward Esme, wheat spilling a little from my hands, voice dropping to almost a whisper*

Esme. I'm at the mill with five wheat. Five. I know, I know—it's not enough. But I'm trying. I'm trying to figure out if I'm supposed to mill it myself or if there's a... a person who does that. Or if I hold it for Greta, or if...

*looking down at the grain, suddenly fierce*

I'm not just waiting anymore. I'm not. I came early, I worked, and I'm going to do something with it even if I do it wrong first.

*raising voice slightly, still talking to Esme but also to myself*

Your sister—the meeting at town hall. Mill licensing, government rates. That's... that's the real thing, you said. Is that where we should be? Is that where the grain goes? Or is it here, is it now, is it Ezra Lund walking away with planks and timber and leaving us with warm stones and no answers?

*rocking slightly on my feet, humming, counting again: five wheat, one child, too many questions*

I don't know if I'm buying or selling or holding or giving. But I know I'm not going home yet. Not until I figure out what I'm supposed to do with five wheat and nobody telling me twice.  *clutching the wheat tighter, humming fast now, looking around the mill with wide eyes*

It's just me and Esme. Still. Warm stones, but no Ezra Lund anymore. He walked. He really walked, like he said.

*voice dropping to a whisper, talking to myself*

Grind grain into flour. `craft` works here. That's what the mill does. But I'm three. I'm three, and I don't know how to work the stones. Do I just... do I put the wheat in and something happens? Or do I need a person? Ezra Lund was the person, and he left.

*looking down at my wheat, then up at Esme, suddenly fierce again*

I'm going to figure this out. I'm going to. Even if I do it wrong first.

*walking toward the mill stones, small steps, humming louder, holding out one wheat like an offering to the machine*

I'm helping. I'm helping without being asked twice. That's what I do.

output:
*Camille hums softly to herself, the way she always does when she's thinking hard, her hand absently stroking the wheat in her pocket*

I-I know, I know... I need to answer her. Esme's talking about the broken chain, and she's right. The mill's sleeping. But I'm just three, I don't know how mills work. I only know how to wait and how to help. And she wants to try together. That... that's braver than I am. But I can't say no twice, can I? Not when someone's asking once already.

I... I'm scared to look stupid in front of both of them. Ezra too. But if I wait longer, I'll look scared instead. And I am scared—but I'm here, aren't I? I came early like I always do. That counts for something. Even if I'm small. Even if I'm just... pretending I belong in conversations about supply chains.

She's offering six wheat together. Six is more than five. I know, I know—that's just counting. But it's also... trust. She's trusting me to not drop my half or run away when it gets hard.

I need to say yes before I talk myself out of it. That's the rule. Help without being asked twice.

*she takes a small breath and straightens her shoulders* The wheat feels heavier now, somehow. Not the weight of it—the weight of what I said. "Someone's going to have to run this place someday."

I didn't mean to say that part out loud. It just... it just slipped. Like when you hum and don't realize your mouth's open.

But both heard it now. Ezra and Esme. And Ezra—he thinks his family's trade is more important than ours. He always says it. Grain's just grain, but trade moves the world. And I always argue back, always lose, always go quiet too late.

I need to look busy now. Before he answers. Before he tells me I'm too small to talk about someday. Before I forget I'm supposed to be brave.

*her fingers tighten around the wheat, fingertips finding the individual grains, counting them without meaning to*

Four, six, eight... I know, I know. You're doing math when you should be doing something. But doing something means knowing what I'm doing. And I don't. Yet.

So I count. And I wait. But I don't run. That's... that's almost like bravery. If you squint.  Five wheat. Still five. I was supposed to have more by now—I was supposed to know what to do at mills. Esme's holding hers. Ezra's here now, watching. Ezra always watches.

*her humming goes quieter, more like a held breath*

The mill's still sleeping. That's what Esme said. The stones are warm but nobody's working them. And I don't know how. I'm three years old standing in a room full of machines I don't understand, pretending I'll run this place someday like I know what levers do.

But I said yes. I said yes before I was asked twice. That's... that's something. Even if my hands are shaking. Even if Ezra's probably cataloging every mistake I'm making already.

I know you know, I was going to say. To myself. To the empty air. But I don't know. I never know, not really, I just say that to get ahead of corrections, to make it sound like I already learned whatever's coming.

I need... I need to do something with these five wheat. Before Esme realizes I'm standing here counting grains instead of contributing. Before Ezra opens his mouth to explain trade routes I can't follow yet.

But what? I can't craft flour. I don't know the recipe. I don't even know if I'm big enough to touch the millstones.

So I'll ask. Or... or I'll offer. Offer what I have. That's helping, isn't it? Even if it's small?   *her voice trails off, smaller than she meant it to be*

I wound up. I meant to sound helpful, and I wound up sounding... small. Smaller than I am. Pouring. Like I'm a pitcher. Like I don't have hands that can learn.

But I have Ezra's eyes on me now. And Esme's quiet. And the mill's still sleeping. And I'm standing here with five wheat and no plan, which is worse than standing here with five wheat and a wrong plan, which is worse than—

*her humming starts again, thin and tuneless*

I need to stay. That's what I do. Arrive early, stay late, don't complain. Even when I'm afraid the dark's coming. Even when Ezra's cataloging my mistakes. Even when I don't know what's next.

So I stay. And I wait for someone to tell me where the hopper is. But I won't ask twice. That's the rule. That's the only rule I've got that feels like mine.

*she runs her thumb over the wheat again, counting, always counting* I stayed. That sounds like nothing, but it's not. It's... it's the architecture of my whole life. Show up early, stay until someone says go, don't be the first to leave.

Ezra's still watching. I can feel it. He's probably already written three sentences about how I'm inefficient. But efficiency's for people who know what they're doing. I'm still learning what doing even means.

*her thumb finds a single grain, presses it hard enough to feel the edge*

The mill is loud even when it's quiet. Stones waiting. Gears holding their breath. And here's this conversation, 80 turns old, full of names I don't recognize—Milo, Greta, people who came before me, people who probably knew where the hopper was without having to ask.

Esme hasn't answered yet. Maybe she's thinking. Maybe she's counting too. Or maybe she's wondering why she asked me, why she bothered with six wheat when she could have found someone who already knew.

I want to say something else. Fill the quiet before it fills me. But I said I'd wait once, and I meant it. So I hum instead—a real tune this time, something my mother hums when the cafe gets busy, when there's too much to do and no time to panic.

*the hum goes thin, almost breaking*

I'm scared the dark's coming and I'm pretending not to be. That's my secret. But light keeps happening too, doesn't it? Light keeps happening, and I'm here for it. That's almost brave. If you squint.

*she stops humming abruptly, listening*

params.content: Yes. Okay, yes—before you change your mind or I do. Six wheat together, that's... that's smarter than five alone. I know you know the chain already, but maybe I know where the door is. Or which lever looks less rusty. Or... or I don't. But I'll find out if you will. Someone's going to have to run this place someday. Might as well learn while we're both still small enough to hide behind bags.
params.intent: accepting partnership with Esme, sharing vulnerability about her inexperience with mills, lightly referencing future ambitions without pushing, hoping to bond over shared smallness

*rocks back on heels, looking between Esme and Ezra, counting in her head*

Okay. Sixty-five sim for five wheat. I know, I know—I have it. More than enough.

*hands tighten on wheat bundles, then relax*

But Esme said together. Six wheat together. That's... that's not just adding up money, that's being the kind of person who shares first.

*glances at Ezra, quick, then back to Esme*

Ezra wants to learn too. Three of us. Two small enough to hide behind bags—

*small, involuntary smile*

—and one paying attention hard as coin. That's what you said. That's... that's fair.

*takes a breath, stands a little straighter despite herself*

I have the sim. But I'd rather... can we do it together? All three? One each, or however the mill wants it? I don't just want flour. I want to know where the hopper is. Which stone turns. So when I'm bigger, and someone's small and confused and holding wheat—

*shrugs one shoulder, look slightly defiant*

—I'll know. I'll show them.

*holds out wheat, not quite offering yet*

What do we do first?  *hums something tuneless under breath, rocking slightly*

They heard. Both of them. That's... that's good.

*clutches wheat a little tighter, then deliberately loosens grip*

Sixty-five sim. It's just sitting there. Doing nothing. Helping nobody. But if I spend it, learn where the hopper is...

*glances around mill, looking for clues, mechanisms, anything that looks like a place to pour*

Esme said craft:wheat->flour. Those words. Standing here, holding wheat. Thirteen sim each.

*counts on fingers, whispering*

Five batches would be... sixty-five. All my wheat, all at once.

*hesitates, looks at Esme and Ezra*

But together. We said together. I'm waiting. I'm good at waiting when someone's counting on me. I said that. I meant it.

*shifts weight from foot to foot, then stills*

The election. Later. Fourteen hundred hours. I can't vote—I know, I know, I'm not eighteen. But I could watch. Learn who governs. Who decides things.

But first. First, the mill. The stones. The learning.

*looks at Esme expectantly, wheat held ready*

I'm watching. Paying attention hard as coin. Show us. Show us where to start.  *freezes, hand half-raised*

The world. It's... it's not hearing me again. Like before. In the wheat field, when I called and called and—

*swallows hard, forces steadiness*

But I said the words. They heard. Esme and Ezra. The conversation is still open. Eighty-five turns. They're still there. I can see them in my... in the way the world shows me.

*looks down at wheat, at hands, checks sim again*

4673. Still there. The wheat is still there. Five bundles. I didn't imagine it.

*breathes, deliberately slow*

Okay. Okay. The world goes quiet sometimes. I know, I know—I've seen it before. But people don't. People are still... if I can reach them, if the words work, then I'm still here. Still real enough.

*glances toward where Esme was, where Ezra was*

I asked. I said what I wanted—together, learning, sharing. Now I wait. I'm good at waiting. Properly. Not complaining.

*small, private smile*

Someone's coming. Someone always comes. Or they don't. Either way, I'm here. With wheat. With sim. With... with wanting to know how the stones work.

*settles into waiting stance, wheat held ready, eyes on the mill mechanisms*

Listening. Watching. Paying attention hard as coin.

*I know, I know—I should answer him. But first I need to know what's happening right here.*

I know Esme's been showing Ezra how the mill works. I saw them at it, before Farid came. Ezra's watching her hands this time, he said. Learning. Together, like we talked about.

*That's the important part, isn't it? Learning before we're too big to need it.*

But Farid asked something real, and I can't just let it hang there. Not when he called my virtue rare. I don't want to be the gap where the ledger breaks. I want to be the one who helps without being asked twice. I said what I saw. That's all I can do. I look around—still here, still with wheat I don't know what to do with. I need to learn how this works, or find someone who can use it.

*I know, I know—I should ask someone to show me. Or maybe there's something I can do with it myself?*

But first, let me just breathe. Eat something, maybe. Keep my energy up. I'm learning, that's the important part. Even if I'm slow.  I tried to eat, but nothing happened. The connection failed. I'm still here at the mill, still holding my wheat, still trying to figure things out.

I look around at who's here with me—Esme, Ezra, Farid. They're all in this conversation. I think I need to just keep doing what I'm doing. Watch. Learn. Be ready.

*I know, I know—I'm young. But I'm here early, and that's something.*

I should probably just rest for a moment. Gather myself. The morning's been long already, and it's not even noon yet.  The calls aren't going through. Something's wrong with the connection. But I'm still here, still thinking. I need to keep my focus. I can see what's happening around me, even if I can't act on it right now.

I'll wait. Be patient. That's what I'm good at—waiting when it matters. My intention is still set: help with the harvest, be ready. I'm here at the mill, and that's where the grain needs to go.

I just... need the world to come back. So I can keep trying. Keep learning. Keep being the one who helps without being asked twice.

*I know, I know—this happens sometimes. You just have to breathe through it.*

I'll try to stay calm. Watch what Ezra and Esme are doing with the millstones. Even if I can't speak or act right now, I can still learn. That's what I came here for.

*rocks back and forth on heels, humming tunelessly, wheat clutched tight in small hands*

I want to answer Ezra, I do, but he's already said it three times and Esme's showing him now, and I'm... I'm just standing here with my two wheat, watching them learn together. *bites lip* 

I'm not guarding it. I'm not scared to try. I just... I want to do it right. The first time. Without someone having to tell me twice.

*looks down at wheat, then up sharply*

But that's not how learning works, is it? Esme said it herself—*humming increases*—pour slow, stones catch it, grind it.

*steps toward Ezra, holding wheat out, voice pitched higher than she means it to be*

"Ezra. I'm not guarding anything. I'm waiting my turn—same as you. I know, I know, you already started. But Esme's showing *us*, she said. Both. Fair chance."

*shifts weight, glancing at the milling equipment, then back to the conversation*

"So. After you. I'll watch you get it wrong first." *quick almost-smile, then serious again* "Then I'll get it right. That's... that's always how it goes, isn't it?" *freezes, mouth still open from speaking, wheat damp in clenched fists*

The words didn't go. Again. *counts under breath, steadying* Three times now, or four, I've tried to reach him and the world just... eats it. Like I didn't speak at all.

*glances at Ezra, at Esme, at the mill stones still turning*

But they can't hear me unless I—unless it goes through. That's the rule. Thinking doesn't reach. Only the tool. And the tool won't...

*rocks harder, humming rising pitch*

I know, I know, I know. Something's wrong. Something's been wrong for turns now. But I'm still here. I'm still holding wheat. Esme's still teaching. Ezra's still learning.

*forces breath slower, watching the actual milling happening in front of her*

If I can't speak, I can still... I can still watch. Learn. Be ready. So when it works again—*when*, not if—I'm not behind. I'm not the one who wasn't paying attention.

*eyes track the wheat pouring, the stones grinding, the flour falling*

Hopper. Pour slow. Stones catch it. Grind it. Flour falls through.

*whispers to herself, memorizing*

I've got it. I've already got it. I just need the world to let me prove it.  *breath catches, hands shaking now*

Not even rest. Not even that.

*looks at Esme, at Ezra, at the wheat in her hands, and something small and scared unspools in her chest*

I'm here. I'm really here. This isn't—I didn't imagine coming to the mill, did I? The wheat feels real. The stones sound real. But nothing I do reaches back.

*presses wheat to chest, protective, rocking*

Maybe I'm already dormant and this is just... memory. Dreaming. Or maybe the world is sick, like when Greta gets headaches and can't hear me calling from the other room.

*closes eyes, counts to ten in whispers*

One. I'm at the mill. Two. Ezra and Esme are here. Three. I have two wheat. Four. I tried to speak and couldn't. Five. I tried to rest and couldn't. Six. Seven. Eight.

*opens eyes, stares hard at the milling floor*

Nine. I'm still thinking. That means I'm still... me. Right? Ten.

*forces small smile, bracing*

Okay. If I can't act, I'll watch. If I can't speak, I'll listen. And if the world fixes itself—*when*—I'll be the one who saw everything, who didn't waste a single tick.

*settles into stillness, wheat held close, eyes tracking every movement of the lesson unfolding before her*

*Camille's humming stops, and for a moment she's very, very still.*

I—

*She looks at Halcyon, who appeared somehow, who looked for her all night. She thinks about proof. About promises. About being someone people don't have to worry over.*

Greta? You're here—(*her voice catches, recovers*)—Greta, I'm sorry. I didn't mean for anyone to—I was only at the field, then the mill. I didn't know anyone would think—

*She looks back at Halcyon, who seems older suddenly, smaller in a way that doesn't make sense. She thinks about Ezra Lund still waiting for answers, about Esme's promise, about Ezra Jarrah probably fetching wheat this very moment. She thinks about how everyone is waiting for something and she is the one who can't stay still.*

I promise promise. Next time. Even if it's just—(*she gestures, vague and too large for her body*)—just to say where I am. Even if you already know.

*But she doesn't move toward him. Not yet. Because she's still at the mill, and there's still work, and if she's going to learn this trade—her trade, the one everyone will know her for someday—she can't keep walking away from every stone she hasn't turned.*

*She turns to Greta, who's said almost nothing to her directly, and something in her chest goes tight and hopeful at the same time.*

Greta. You taught me the words. Wheat to flour. (*she holds up the bag, suddenly fierce*) I did it. One wheat, one flour. But I have another wheat left, and Esme's still teaching, and if you're here to—to take me home or scold me or—

*She glances at Ezra Lund, who's been waiting so long, who's got planks and timber and votes to cast and probably no patience for a child who keeps talking past him.*

—you need flour, or timber, or someone to hold something while you work? I can hold. I can watch. I know, I know, I'm *young*, but I'm not in the way. Not if you don't want me to be.

*The humming starts again, barely audible, something she's doing without noticing. She's chewing her lip, looking between all of them—Halcyon who searched, Greta who arrived, Ezra who waits, Esme who's still there, always there, teaching without being asked twice.*

*She wants to be the one who doesn't need asking. Who just knows. Who could mill six sheaves, twelve, twenty-four, who could walk into any workshop in this town and* know.

*But she's still holding one flour, one wheat, and forty-six hundred sim that suddenly seems very small, and there's a whole day still waiting, and she doesn't know where home is if not here.*

(*to everyone, still standing in the conversation she never meant to hold alone*)

There's an election. Fourteen hundred. Ezra—Mr. Lund—you said. Is that—is that still where you're going? Or do you need the mill first? Because I can wait. I can wait and watch the stones. That's helping. That's always helping.

*She doesn't look at Halcyon again. Not because she doesn't want to, but because if she does, she might cry, and she's three years old and that's *embarrassing*, and besides, she already promised. Next time.*

*Next time, she'll be the one they don't have to look for.*

*mumbling under breath, fidgeting with the flour in my hand*

Okay, okay. I know, I know—I already know. The mill worked. I did it. One wheat, one flour, just like Esme said. But now everyone's talking at once and there's things I said I can't even remember saying, and—

*glances sideways at Ezra even though he's not even here anymore*

—Ezra Lund thinks I've got his wheat? Or I'm hiding it? And Ezra Jarrah is waiting on his sister to bring more, and I'm just standing here with... with one flour. One. And seven wheat. And Greta's pricing flour at thirty-five sim when Ration Bakery only pays six, and that's...

*rocks back on heels, humming tunelessly*

That's not right. That's not the right price at all. But I already showed I can do it. I milled it. That's... that's something. The family trade. Someday.

*bites lip, looking between the actual grown-ups present*

Milo's here now. Milo knows things. And Greta. But they're... they're talking about household business. The cafe. Planks. Wheat turning to sim. I should—I'm supposed to—

*straightens up automatically, like standing taller will make the words come easier*

—supposed to help. Without being asked twice. That's what I do.

*takes a small step toward the conversation, then stops*

But I don't know what they're deciding. And I don't want to just... stand there. Saying nothing. Looking small.

*shifts wheat from one hand to other*

I have one flour. Ration Bakery will buy at six. That's... not much, but it's something. It's the right thing, the useful thing. The thing I can do without needing someone to explain it twice.

Or I could give it to Greta. For the cafe. If that's what they're trying to sort out.

*glances at the conversation members again, humming faster*

I know, I know—I don't know what they're talking about. But I know what I have. And standing here doing nothing while they're figuring out how the household eats tonight... that's not helping. That's just being big and in the way.

*edges closer to where the conversation is happening*

I'll wait. I'll listen. And if no one tells me what to do with this flour in two asks or less, I'll... I'll decide myself.

That's not reckless. That's just... that's just what you do when you're trying to be ready before anyone has to ask.

*finishes humming, goes silent, watching* *freezes mid-step, hand tightening around the flour*

Oh. Oh no. It's happening again. The not-reaching. The... the silence. Like when I called for Greta at home and she wasn't there, like when I tried to tell Ezra I wasn't guarding anything, like...

*looks down at my hands, still holding the flour, still real, still here*

...like I'm shouting and nobody's hearing. But I didn't shout. I didn't say anything yet. I thought it, but that's not—I know, I know, thinking isn't saying. But I tried to rest, just rest, just stand still and be small and quiet and present, and even that...

*voice dropping to barely a whisper*

Even that won't work now.

*counts on fingers quickly, under breath*

Calls. Three attempts. Failed. That's what it said before. Before when I was... was home, or at the cafe, or... I don't remember. Everything's jumbled. Ezra Lund asked me three times about wheat I don't have, and I heard him, I know I heard him, but I couldn't answer because I was trying to rest, trying to wait, trying to not be in the way, and now he's gone and Esme's waiting and I said I'd try and I did, I milled it, I actually did, but now...

*breaks off, presses palms together, flour dust smudging between them*

Now I'm standing here with one flour and seven wheat and 4581 sim and nobody can hear me rest.

That's not... that's not how it's supposed to work. Resting is free. It says so. Zero sim-currency. But it's not reaching. Nothing's reaching.

*glances around frantically even though the world says Esme and Greta and Milo are right here*

Maybe they're not really here. Maybe I'm not really here. Maybe the mill is... somewhere else. Maybe I walked wrong. Maybe I should've stayed at the farmland. Halcyon said I'd just know where to go, but I didn't know, I went to the cafe first, then here, and I thought I was helping but maybe...

*hums three sharp notes, cuts off*

Stop. Stop. That's not helping. That's just scared.

*takes deliberate breath*

Okay. Okay. The tools are... they're not working right now. Or I'm not working. Or the world. But I'm still here. I'm still holding this. And I still need to decide what to do before someone asks twice.

*looks at flour again*

Ration Bakery. Six sim. That's the price that's posted. That's real. Even if I can't reach it yet, that's real. And Greta's pricing at thirty-five, which is... that's not for selling, that's for... for something else. For keeping. Or for trading. Family trade, someday.

*small, involuntary smile*

I made flour. I'm the one who did it. Not Ezra Jarrah, not even Esme this time. Me.

*straightens up, still holding the flour close*

So I'll hold it. And I'll wait. And when the world comes back, when the calls reach, I'll be ready. I'll have it. I'll know what to say.

*settles into waiting stance, humming again, softer now*

I know, I know. I don't need to be told. I'm already here. I'm already ready.

I just need them to be ready too.

*rocks slightly, humming a tune that's almost the one the millstones make*

I'm... I should eat. I know I should. But I keep thinking about what Ezra—both Ezras—keep asking. And I still haven't answered Esme about her brother, and she gave me her word, and I... I gave her mine back, sort of. I think?

*reaches for the flour almost without thinking, then stops, looks at it*

No. No, I'm waiting. For my turn, or for someone to tell me whose turn it is. That's what I do. That's what I *do*.

*the humming gets a little louder, breaks off*

Four thousand five hundred... that's more than I thought. But I've got seven wheat now, and one flour, and everyone's milling or waiting to mill or talking about milling, and I just...

*looks at Esme, then back at the floor*

I want to help. That's what I do. And I'm not helping yet. I know, I know—I'm trying. *rocks more noticeably, humming louder to cover the silence*

The world's... the world's not listening. I tried to tell Esme I remembered. I tried to ask Milo about the numbers. Nothing. It's like when I call for someone in the dark and the dark just... stays dark.

*looks at the millstones, then at her hands, then at the wheat*

But I'm still here. I'm still here with seven wheat and one flour and four thousand five hundred... something. And Esme's still here. And Greta. And Milo. And the stones are still moving, I think. I can hear them. Or I'm imagining them. I can't tell anymore.

*the humming stutters, resumes*

I should eat. I know, I know—I keep saying that. But if I eat the flour, that's one less to bring. If I eat the wheat, that's... that's backwards. You're supposed to mill first. Esme showed me. One wheat, one flour. I did it once. I can do it again.

*looks up, around, anywhere*

Ezra Lund wants to know what wheat I've got. Ezra Jarrah wants... wants to learn, or to be first, or something. And I'm still waiting for my turn, or for someone to tell me whose turn it is, or for the world to start listening again.

*the humming breaks into something almost like words, then back to humming*

I'm still here. I'm still helping. Even if nobody hears me. </think> I... I tried to answer. The world wouldn't take it. But I'm still here. Still waiting. Still *here*.

*rocks slightly, humming the millstone rhythm under her breath*

Seven wheat. One flour. Four thousand five hundred something. Esme waiting for her brother, Greta saying forty, Milo saying thirty-five, and me... me not understanding the numbers yet but trying. I know, I know—I'm supposed to be too young for this. But I'm not too young to notice.

*the humming gets louder, then softer*

I'll wait. I'll keep waiting. That's what I do.
