I feel the panic rising in my chest like when the lights go out and I pretend I'm brave. The world keeps slipping away—my words won't stick, my calls won't reach. I have 7 wheat and 1 flour weighing down my small hands, and my family is here at the mill but I can't make them hear me.

I look down at the wheat kernels, rough and golden. I know, I know—I'm supposed to help, supposed to be useful, supposed to take over the family trade someday. But right now I'm a child standing in a mill with grown-up problems, and the tools won't answer.

The household needs 360 sim for upkeep and the head tax takes 120 more. Greta's words echo in my memory—that we have cushion for two days, maybe three if we tighten. I ate something I shouldn't have. Or someone took my wheat. Or I traded it without seeing. There's flour in my hands now where wheat used to be, and that should be good but I'm not sure how it happened.

I clutch the remaining wheat tighter. My fingers know how to hold small things carefully—that's what I do. I'm careful with anything softer than me. But Esme is gone to fetch her brother, and Ezra is... somewhere... and I'm standing in the middle of a mill with my parents watching me be useless.

The fear of being different crawls up my spine. Every other kid in town knows what they're doing. I arrive early, I hum when concentrating, I say "I know, I know" before anyone tells me anything—but knowing the words doesn't mean I understand the work.

I need to stop trying to speak into the void and just... be here. Present. Small and careful and waiting for the world to let me back in.

If I can't call out, I'll just hold what I have and watch. That's what I do. I watch until I understand. I help without being asked twice.

The wheat presses against my palm. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Still there. Still mine. Still something I can do with my hands when the words won't work.

I wait. </think> [Camille stands very still at the mill, holding her wheat close, small fingers counting and recounting the kernels she can still feel. She doesn't speak—can't make herself heard—but she watches her parents with wide eyes, waiting for the world to let her back in.]

*rocks back and forth on her toes, humming under her breath, studying the millstones with the intensity of someone memorizing the grain of stone itself*

I know, I know—Papa already told me.

*glances at Esme, who's still waiting, then back at Milo, who's selling flour at thirty-five while he tells me to mill more*

One wheat became one flour became... one wheat gone, one flour here. Now four flour, four wheat. Papa says walk out with three flour and coin, or two flour and more coin, but he sells flour at thirty-five Esme sells flour at... nobody says.

*chews her lip, small fingers counting silently*

The ledger. The ledger doesn't break if names are said. That's what I told Mr. Ravensworth. That's what I *know*.

*straightens, suddenly looking older than three for exactly half a second*

Papa said not to wait for older. Esme's showing, and I'm showing first. That's helping.

*turns to Milo, voice careful but carrying* *blinks, fingers drifting to her mouth, suddenly small again*

The words didn't... the words didn't go.

*looks around the mill—Esme waiting, Milo selling, the stones grinding, grinding, grinding*

I know, I know. It's my turn. It's been my turn.

*shifts from foot to foot, humming louder now—a tuneless hum that means she's concentrating*

Papa said sell five wheat for forty. Mill two wheat to flour. Walk out with three flour, forty sim. But I have four flour already. I milled... I milled when I shouldn't have, or should have, or—

*glances at Esme, protective instinct warring with wanting-to-help*

If I sell wheat, I'm trading. If I mill, I'm... learning. Esme's still waiting for her brother, and I'm still here, and Papa said act when I see the path.

*takes a breath that wobbles slightly*

I see the path. I think I do. It's just... it's just two paths. And I need to pick one before the stones stop singing.

*looks down at her small hands, calculating again, mouthing numbers*

Four flour. Four wheat. Sixty-five sim in pocket, not forty. Papa said forty but I have more, I helped, I watched, I learned without asking twice.

*chews her lip harder*

Sell five wheat for forty. Mill one more wheat to flour. Walk out with five flour, forty sim, one wheat. Or mill two wheat, walk out with six flour, no sim, two wheat.

Or sell the flour. Sell flour at... at thirty-five? But Papa's selling at thirty-five. I can't... I know, I know, I can't undercut Papa.

*rocks back and forth, the humming returning*

The Ration Bakery buys flour at six. That's... that's not right. That's not right at all. Six is less than thirty-five. Six is...

*trails off, confused, momentarily lost*

I don't understand the numbers. I don't understand why Esme's brother hasn't come. I don't understand why I'm still standing here when Papa said act.

*straightens again, decision crystallizing*

I know what I know. I know the stones. I know watching. I know helping without asking twice.

*turns to face the mill equipment, small hands reaching*  *hand falls back to her side, fingers curling into her palm*

Nothing. Nothing moves.

*looks at Esme, eyes wider now, the flinch showing*

The mill's not... the mill's not listening. Or I'm not. I know, I know, I'm saying it wrong, or thinking it wrong, or—

*turns full circle, searching for what's changed, what broke*

Papa's still selling. Esme's still waiting. The stones are still turning. But I can't... I can't touch them anymore.

*breathes out, shaky, then deliberately slows the breath*

Okay. Okay. When the biggest kid picks on the smallest, you say something. When the mill won't answer, you... you wait. You watch. You don't break things by pushing harder.

*settles back onto her heels, humming resuming, softer now*

I know, I know. I'm still here. That's the first thing. I'm still here, and I'm still watching, and Esme's still showing me how to wait.

*glances at Milo, calculation in her small face*

Papa said act when I see the path. Maybe... maybe I don't see the whole path yet. Maybe I'm only supposed to see the next stone.

*rocking slightly, watching the millstones grind*

Four flour. Four wheat. Sixty-five sim. And Esme, waiting.

That's what's real. That's what's now. The rest... the rest can wait until the speaking works again.

*settles into waiting, patient as only a child who arrives early to everything can be*

*drops my last wheat on the stone, watches it roll, catches it before it falls*

I know, I know, Papa said wait. But Esme's here, and I'm here, and Ezra's... somewhere being EzraProbably better at everything as usual.

*fidgets with the wheat between small fingers, looks up at Esme*

"Esme. Your brother's not back. Papa's selling flour at thirty-five now, and I... I've got seven flour, and one wheat, and I'm—I know, I know, I'm supposed to wait. But waiting feels like letting him win. Again." *stands frozen, wheat in hand, mouth open from words that went nowhere*

The mill stones keep turning. I can hear them. But my voice... my hands... nothing answers.

*pushes the wheat into my pocket, suddenly needing to hold something solid*

It's happening again. Like when I tried to tell Ezra his family trade wasn't better, just different. The words go out, but they don't land.

*looks at Esme, really looks at her—can't tell if she heard or if I'm just a girl standing quiet in a noisy room*

I'm still here. I'm—I'm still here. That's what matters. That's what Papa's ledger would say. Present. Accounted for.

*rocks on my heels, hums under my breath without meaning to*

The wheat in my pocket. Eight flour total, if the world wakes up. Or seven and one wheat, if it doesn't. Either way, I'm... I'm holding something. That's more than nothing.

*wants to say more, waits for the stones to stop laughing at her*

I feel a finger of cold tracing down my spine seeing Esme still here—just us now, me and her and the silence, and Papa's voice still echoing about pinky promises. I know, I know I told him I was watching, not guarding, but watching feels like waiting and waiting feels like losing. Especially with Ezra somewhere out there fetching more wheat while I'm standing here with eight flour heavy in my hands.

The election is today. I'm too young to vote, but I arrive early to everything out of habit—like I arrived early to the mill, like I'm early to every thought about what I'm supposed to be doing with my life. The family trade. Take it over someday. But what if I'm not good enough? What if Ezra's better at this than me? What if I mill and mill and mill and it's never enough?

Right now I need to—to do something. I'm holding eight flour. Papa's selling at thirty-five and I'm... I'm just standing here with my hands full. The Ration Bakery will buy flour at six. The Ration Bakery will buy. I should sell. I should do something useful. But I've been waiting for Esme or Ezra or someone to tell me what's right.

No. I know, I know—I say that before I'm told anything. So I should know by now. I should act. Eight flour in my hands, and if I don't sell them, they'll sit there, and sitting things don't help anyone.

I'll sell to the Ration Bakery. They're at cb01. I'll have to move there. But first, let me breathe—and write this down, because I've been crafting without writing, and better is cheaper, and if I'm going to take over the family trade I need to be better.

Let me start by selling the flour, then. And I'll note that I need to learn the path from mill to bakery so I don't have to think so hard next time. I'll sell what's in my hand, move to where they are, and make the trade. That's helping. That's doing without being asked twice. </think> I'll sell the flour I milled to the Ration Bakery, and move there to do it. And I need to set an intention—I'm helping the household, I'm learning the trade, I'm not waiting anymore.

I need to think carefully about what's urgent right now. I'm at the mill with 8 flour in hand. My papa Milo spoke to me—he wants me to mark down my counts: 4 flour, 4 wheat, and 1 waiting. But I've actually made 7 flour with my one remaining wheat. He's right that I should keep my word to Esme.

But there's more pressing business. The household needs money for upkeep—a 360 sim bill that my family has to pay. I work for my living, and they need me to contribute. But also, deeply, I'm uneasy because... because Ezra always wins. And now I'm waiting again.

I need to sell this flour to help my household. Ration Bakery is buying flour at 6 sim, and I have 8 flour—that's 48 sim, plus the 4,467 I already have. That's important. But I promised Esme I'd wait for her to learn milling first.

*She isn't here. Her brother went somewhere and she hasn't come back. I heard Delphine Quintero saying something about trading wheat with Kenji Jarrah.*

I... I've been waiting and waiting. Papa says wait isn't letting anyone win—it's keeping your word. But I've kept my word. For turns and turns. And the household bill is real.

Let me first check who is actually here with me, and what's for sale. I need to sell this flour to help my household. Esme IS here. And Delphine. The conversation shows what I thought—Esme's been waiting for her brother, but Ezra left and hasn't come back. I want to help her, I do... but I also need to help my household.

Let me think about what I need to do:

1. I promised Esme I'd wait so she could learn milling
2. But the household needs money—360 sim for upkeep
3. I have 8 flour I could sell to Ration Bakery at 6 sim each = 48 sim (not enough for the whole bill, but something)

I feel torn. Papa told me that wait isn't keeping anyone from winning—it's keeping my word. I've kept my word. But also... I need to contribute.

Let me say something to Esme. Maybe she can come with me, or maybe she's had enough waiting too.

Actually, wait. Let me think about this differently. The record says I'm "uneasy" and trying to "Deal with what is hanging over me." What if... what if Esme doesn't want to mill anymore? She's been waiting so long for Ezra to bring wheat, and he hasn't come back. Maybe she's ready to go do something else.

Let me ask her. But also—I need to be practical. I'll tell her I'm going to sell flour to help my household, and she could come if she wants, or I could teach her quickly right now before I go. Actually, Papa said I shouldn't teach her at the mill because I'm not employed there. But...

I know, I know—I'm overthinking this. Let me just talk to her.  The call failed again. This has been happening a lot. Maybe I should just act. My intention was to sell 8 flour to Ration Bakery. Maybe I should just do that now—go there and sell it. I can tell Esme later that I had to help my family.

Let me move to Ration Bakery (business:cb01).   Everything is failing. Let me try to rest and see if that helps. I see. The system is having trouble. Let me try something different.

*Camille hums softly, the tune wobbling as she stands at the mill, clutching her 8 bags of flour. She looks at Esme, still waiting, still patient—too patient, maybe, like she's been too patient with Ezra all these years.*

I can't seem to reach the world. Everything I try just... fails. I wanted to tell Esme I have to go sell flour for my family. I wanted to move to Ration Bakery and help pay the 360 sim bill. But my words aren't carrying, my feet won't walk.

*She squeezes the flour bags tighter. The unease from before—that "what is hanging over me"—she knows what it is now. It's the fear that she'll wait forever, keeping promises that nobody else keeps, while Ezra wins again and her family struggles.*

Maybe... maybe I should try something simpler. Not moving, not talking—just checking what I'm supposed to be doing. Let me recall my goals.  I have one goal: "Deal with what is hanging over me" with priority 4, urgency "now." It's been held for 36 turns. My safety need is at 0.7, which is high—I feel unsafe.

I know what the unease is. It's the household bill. It's Ezra always winning. It's waiting and waiting while things get harder. I need to act.

Papa told me I've got seven flour and one wheat because I made it so. That's work done proper. But waiting... waiting isn't helping.

Let me try to do something concrete. I'll try to sell my flour. The price is posted—Ration Bakery buys at 6 sim. I'll try to sell all 8.

*I hum softly, my fingers counting in my pocket even though there's nothing there to count anymore*

I sold the flour. I did it. Papa's words are... they're sitting in me, heavy as stones. "Wait's keeping your word to a friend who kept hers to you." But Esme never answered me, and I had to go, and now I'm here and she's there and I don't know if I kept my word or broke it.

*twists the hem of my shirt, back and forth*

I have 4,506 sim now. That's... that's good. That's helping. But I was supposed to teach Esme. She was waiting so long, and I said I would, and then I didn't.

*looks around the empty bakery*

Nobody's here. Nobody heard me leave. Nobody heard me try to explain. 

I should find Papa. He's at the mill, or he was. He'll tell me if I did right. He always tells me, even when I don't want to hear it. And I need to... I need to understand what "keeping your word" means when your word was keeping you from helping your own household.

*starts toward the door, then pauses*

But I also need to not make the same mistake twice. If I'm going to keep helping, I need to know what I'm walking into. What this place even is, besides where I just sold our flour for less than Papa wanted.

 *exhales slowly*

Ration Bakery. That's where I am. And they're buying flour at 6, which is... that's why I only got 48 for 8 flour. Papa wanted 35 per flour, but that was selling to people, not to a bakery that needs to make bread and sell it again.

*counts on fingers, muttering*

Eight times six is forty-eight. That's... that's math. That's what happened.

*looks at the empty room, then toward where the mill would be*

I need to find Papa. I need to tell him what I did, and hear if he's angry, and understand why waiting felt like losing even when he says it isn't.

*starts humming, off-key, the same three notes over and over*

I know, I know, I should just go. But I'm scared he's disappointed. And I'm scared I disappointed Esme more.

But standing here won't fix any of it.

  *stumbles a bit as she arrives, catches herself against the wall*

I'm here. I need to look around, find Papa. Or anyone who can tell me if I did right or wrong.

*straightens her shirt, tries to look like she knows what she's doing*

I know, I know, I should have stayed. But I couldn't stay. The bill was coming and I had flour and Esme wasn't answering and...

*trails off, looking for familiar faces*  *sees Esme still there, and her chest tightens*

Esme's still here. She waited. She kept waiting. And I left without teaching her, without even... without even waiting for her to answer me.

*sees Halcyon too, her brother, and doesn't know if she's relieved or more nervous*

Halcyon's here. And Delphine... the grocery clerk. But no Papa. No Milo.

*shifts from foot to foot, humming under her breath*

I should talk to Esme first. I should... I should explain. Or apologize. Or something.

But I also need to find Papa. Greta said—she said things about prices, and I sold at six, and I don't know if that was right.

*walks toward where Esme stands, small and careful*

Esme. I'm... I'm back. I had to go. The household needed the money, and you weren't answering, and I... I know, I know, I said I'd teach you. I said I'd wait. But I couldn't stay anymore.

*looks down at her hands*

I sold the flour for forty-eight. That's... that's six each. Papa wanted thirty-five, but that was for people, not for a bakery.

*glances up, trying to read Esme's face*  *hears the echo of who didn't hear—Ration Bakery isn't here, obviously—and feels the knot in her stomach loosen just slightly*

Esme heard me. Halcyon heard me. Delphine heard me.

*turns toward her brother, suddenly unsure if she's happy to see him or afraid he'll tell Papa what she did*

Halcyon. You're here. I didn't... I didn't know you were coming.

*swallows hard, looks back toward Esme*

I'm waiting. I'll wait for her to answer this time. I won't leave again without... without doing what I said I'd do. Or explaining why I can't.

*hums the three notes, over and over, waiting*

output:
*Camille hums tunelessly, standing at the mill with flour dust still on her hands. The world feels big here, even though she knows it's not. Papa's words are heavy in her ears—"work done proper"—but Halcyon's words are heavier. All night. Looking.*

*She's avoiding looking at Halcyon. She came early, like always, and now she's paying for it because she didn't know where her brother was or what he thought happened. She's never been missing before. She's always just been... there.*

*But Esme is here. Esme who waited. And Ezra, somewhere, not having brought the wheat he promised. The unfairness of it pricks at her—Ezra getting to be the one who breaks promises while she's the one who keeps them.*

*She should answer. Everyone. But the words get stuck because she's three and the world keeps telling her she's small, and sometimes she believes it.* *She fidgets, the hum starting again, quieter now. The words are out but they feel thin. She wants to add something—about being different, about trying not to be, about how being early to everything doesn't help when it means people worry where you've gone.*

*But Esme is waiting too. Esme who kept her word, who waited while Ezra didn't come back. There's something about that Camille understands too well—the waiting, the keeping, the being the one who stays while others go.*

*She should say something to Esme too. Something about pinky promises and who's better at keeping them. But Ezra's name sticks in her throat because she wants to say something about him not coming back, something sharper than she should, and she's afraid if she starts she won't stop.*

*Instead she looks at her hands. Four flour, four wheat, the count. Work done proper. She wants to believe that means something.*  *She knew Ezra wouldn't hear. That was deliberate, maybe. Something she's not ready to say to his face yet. The thought of him at Government Complex—doing what? voting? declaring?—while Esme waited here with nothing, makes her stomach tight.*

*But there's Halcyon still. Halcyon who looked all night. Who thought she was gone forever. The weight of that sits on her shoulders heavier than the flour bags she watched Milo carry.*

*She wants to be brave, like Papa said. Learning early. But bravery feels different when it's your own brother thinking you're lost.*

*She checks her hands again. Still dusty. Still small. But she made seven flour. She made something.*  *She stays. Because leaving now feels like running, and she doesn't run from the big things. Just flinches from them. Just stands still afterward, humming, waiting to see what happens next.*

output:
*Camille hums a little as she watches the millstones grind, then stops abruptly when Delphine speaks about flour moving where it shouldn't. She looks down at her hands, still dusty with flour from the morning's work.*

*She's only three, but she's learned to be careful around adults who speak of debts and double entries. She tucks herself slightly behind the nearest wooden post, making herself smaller than she is, watching Delphine with wide eyes. But when Delphine mentions the farmland—where Papa went—her head comes up sharply.*

*She glances at Esme, who seems uncertain. She glances at Halcyon, her sister, who she's still learning to trust with secrets. The pinky promise matters. Helping without being asked twice matters more.*

I know, I know—I should probably stay put. But Papa went that way, and if Delphine's going to the farmland to find wheat, and Esme's brother might be there too... that's two people I promised things to, isn't it? Even if Esme would understand. Especially if she'd understand.

*She steps out from behind the post, small and determined, and touches Delphine's sleeve to get her attention without raising her voice.*

"I'll walk with you. To the farmland. Papa went for wheat, and Esme's brother—he might be there too. Two buyers, that's what you said. But I don't have eight. I don't have... I sold my flour already. I was helping."

*She looks at Esme, then, earnest and a little guilty.*

"Pinky's still pinky. But helping without being asked twice—that's first. And you don't need me here the same way. You've got Halcyon now. You've got... you've got waiting, and you're good at it. I'm not good at waiting."

*She swallows, and says quickly before anyone can answer:*

"Besides. If I find Papa, I can tell him what I did. With the flour. He asked what I needed, and I didn't know then, but I know now. I need him to know I did it right."

*She offers Delphine her hand—the one that's not covered in mill dust—the way she's seen adults do when they're making a real journey together.* *She keeps her hand out, waiting, small in a world of adults and millstones and debts that write themselves into books she cannot read.*  *She's walking now—small steps to match Delphine's longer ones, if Delphine comes, or alone if she doesn't. Either way, the farmland is where Papa went. The farmland is where answers grow, along with wheat.*

output:
*clutching her hands together tight*

I've walked to the street but I don't see Papa. I see Uncle Takeshi—he's selling flour at thirty, which is... that's less than Papa's thirty-five. And planks at seven, like Papa. Mama always said Uncle Takeshi knows the numbers in his sleep.

*humming low, then catching herself*

I know, I know—Ezra Lund's here too, selling planks and timber. They asked about wheat. I told them I had none, but I didn't know they were HERE now.

*rocking slightly on her heels*

Delphine was going to walk with me to the farmland, but I don't see her either. I just see... all these grown-ups talking about the election and flour and timber and iron. The big conversation. The one with 148 turns already.

*trying to edge closer, small and quiet*

I'm only three-and-a-half hands high in this crowd. I can't even see over Ulrike Greenhow's elbow. But I need to find Papa, or Ezra—Ezra Jarrah, I mean, the one who was meant to bring wheat back for Esme. 

*whispering to herself*

I promised Esme I'd wait. I promised. And then I walked away to sell flour, and I didn't tell Halcyon, and now she's saying promise promise next time and I didn't even SAY goodbye to Esme properly...

*wants to speak to someone but freezes, looking at all the adults*

They're all so tall. So loud. So sure.

Maybe if I just... listen? The conversation's about milling and flour. I know milling. I milled eight flour today. I know, I know—I know how the stones hum when they're working right, and how they scream when something's wrong.

*standing very still, trying to be small enough not to bother anyone*  *flinching slightly, but only at the edges*

Papa's not here. Not in this place. I knew—I knew, I knew he wouldn't be, they're all so loud here, and Papa likes the open where he can see the sky, but I had to ask. Had to try.

*touching her own chest, small*

But they heard me. Ezra Lund heard me. Uncle Takeshi heard, and Uncle Lior, and Ulrike, and Idris. They heard a child talk about milling stones. 

*rocking again, humming under her breath*

I said it right, didn't I? Grain needs hands willing to cut it. The stones scream empty when there's no grain. I know. I know this. Papa taught me before I was this tall—when I could barely reach the hopper, he lifted me up to feel the wheat pour through my fingers like sand, like water, like gold that grows out of dirt.

*looking around, suddenly desperate*

But where IS he? He went for wheat. To the farmland, after he talked about selling flour at thirty-five. I was supposed to wait—I was supposed to stay with Esme, and I didn't, and now I'm here and Papa's there and Halcyon's angry and Mama's scared and I just wanted to HELP—

*voice cracking, but forcing it down*

I know, I know. Crying doesn't find wheat. Crying doesn't sell flour. Crying doesn't make Ezra Jarrah come back with grain for his sister.

*breathing hard, looking at the milling conversation adults again*

They didn't answer me. They heard, but they didn't answer. Grown-ups do that—they let children talk, and they nod, and they keep their own words for later, or for each other.

Maybe... maybe if I'm still? If I stand here small enough, quiet enough, someone will say something about wheat? About who's bringing it? About whether Ezra—either Ezra, Jarrah or Lund—has been seen walking back with grain in their hands?

*wrapping her arms around herself*

Or maybe I should walk. To the farmland. That's where Papa went. That's where Ezra Jarrah was meant to be. That's where Delphine said she'd go with me, but she's not here, and I can't wait anymore. I know, I know—I shouldn't walk alone. I know. But waiting alone on the street isn't better, is it? It's just waiting in a different shape.

*deciding, with something that looks almost like her father's stubbornness*

I'm going to find Papa. Or find Ezra. Or find wheat. All three, if the town's kind today.

*already stepping, already moving*  *already walking - already walking*

I'm walking. I'm already walking. Two ticks left—that's barely time to hum a whole song, barely time to count steps, barely time to remember what I should have said to Esme before I left her waiting by the mill stones.

*humming, counting, trying to stop her hands from shaking*

One tick. Two ticks. Papa's there, or Ezra's there, or the wheat's there, or nobody's there and I'm walking toward empty stalks and empty hands and—

*her voice betraying her*

—I don't want to be alone there either. Not on the farmland. Not where it's open sky and nobody between me and the dark if the dark decides to come early.

*whispering to herself, fierce and frightened*

I pretend not to be. I pretend all the time. Big kids don't fear the dark. Big kids don't need night-lights. Big kids walk wherever they want without asking twice, without being asked twice, without—

*cutting off, humming louder*

I know, I know. I'll see when I get there. The world will tell me when I get there. That's how it works here. You walk, you wait, you arrive, you look around. Then you know. Not before.

*silence, walking, hoping*

*stands at the farmland, fidgeting with her skirt hem, eyes scanning the rows of wheat for Papa's familiar figure—then flinches slightly at the tall folk gathered around, but straightens when she spots Imogen Lund*

I know, I know, I said I'd walk with Delphine. But she's here now, and I... I have to answer. Ezra asked twice. Twice is once too many to ignore.

*steps a little closer to Imogen, trying to make her voice carry without shouting* *eyes widen slightly—Delphine's not here. She thought—she could have sworn they walked together. But the wheat sways and the faces are all tall strangers and she's small here, very small, with Kenji Jarrah selling wheat at eight and Imogen with flour at twelve and she's got neither, only questions*

I know, I know. I should've looked. Should've made sure she was with me before I opened my mouth.

*twists her skirt hem tighter, hums a few notes under her breath—the tune doesn't matter, it's just something to do while she thinks*

Papa. He's here somewhere. He has to be. He went for wheat, and this is where wheat comes from, and if I find him I can tell him what I did—the flour sold, the money in my hand, the prices I learned. He asked what I needed. What I needed was to know I did it right.

*looks again at Kenji Jarrah, at the wheat he's selling. Eight. Same as the price she held in her head. Same as Papa would pay, if he were here*

I don't have eight. Not for wheat. But if I watch, if I learn who sells fair and who might cheat a child... that's helping too. That's the trade. That's what I'll need to take over someday.  *flinches at the note—Papa's not here. Of course he's not here. She knew that, she knew, but seeing it written like that makes her stomach tight*

I know, I know. I should've waited. Should've held my tongue until I knew something worth saying.

*hum-hums under her breath, three quick notes, higher at the end like a question*

Sebastian Petrov heard. Kenji Jarrah too. They know I'm here now, and they know whose girl I am. That's... that's not nothing. In the trade, being known is worth almost as much as wheat.

*touches the coins in her pocket—4481, after selling flour, after all the milling. Enough to buy wheat if she had to. Enough to eat if she needed to. But she's three, and she doesn't eat alone, and the household feeds together or not at all*

Giselle Ingram. Construction company. Idris Solano. More tall folk, watching the child fidget in the wheat-field. I should...

*doesn't finish the thought. Too many eyes. Better to wait, better to watch, better to find Papa or learn what she needs before she promises something else she can't keep*

I'll stand here. Quiet. Humming. Letting them forget I'm small, letting them remember I'm Milo's girl when it matters.

*shifts weight from foot to foot, waiting*

*wrings hands, looking from person to person at the farmland, humming softly under breath*

I know, I know—I asked so many questions and now I'm here and Papa's still not. But Kenji Jarrah has wheat at eight, and I... I have enough. Barely. Four sheaves would be thirty-two, and I have forty-four seventy... no, forty-four seventy-eight.

*glances toward where Kenji stands, then toward the mill direction, then back*

But Papa went for wheat this morning. He must have found some. If I buy now, and he bought too, and we both come home with wheat...

*shifts weight from foot to foot, humming louder*

Delphine wanted two buyers. I'm only one, and I haven't got eight anyway. Not for two. And Esme's still waiting. And Ezra's looking for her, and I've got no right to be here buying when the mill's where I should be helping.

*breathes out, decision settling*

I'm going back. To the mill. If Papa's there, he'll know what I should do. If he's not, I'll watch the stones until someone who knows better comes. I know, I know—that's what I said before. But I mean it now.

*turns toward the mill path, already walking*  *stumbles slightly as the world shifts around her, landing back at the mill—stone walls, grinding sounds, the familiar weight of flour dust in the air*

*exhales sharply, hands still trembling slightly from the jump*

I'm back. I'm back, and I need to—

*looks around quickly for Papa, for Esme, for anyone she knows*

—need to find who I promised to help. Esme was waiting. She was always waiting. And if Ezra found her, or if she's still alone...

*pulls self straighter, humming one steady note to settle nerves*

Pinky promise. I said I'd be back. I said I'd help without being asked twice. That's what matters. That's what always matters.

*steps forward to look for Esme, for Halcyon, for anyone who can tell her what's happened while she was gone*  *catches breath, eyes finding Mama at the mill—Mama, who's always known what to do*

*steps forward quickly, voice dropping to something quieter than the bragging tone from before*

"Mama. I did what Papa said—sold the flour, eight sacks at six. But I went to the farmland after, looking for him, and he's not there. Kenji Jarrah's selling wheat at eight, and I almost bought, but..."

*shifts weight, hands clasping and unclasping*

"...but Papa went for wheat this morning. He must've found some. And I didn't want us both coming home with grain neither of us planned for."

*looks around, searching the faces she doesn't see*

"Mama—where's Esme? And Ezra? I promised her pinky, and I promised I'd be back, and I was gone too long."

*voice tightens, humming starting again despite herself*

"Is she still waiting? Did he find her? I know, I know—I should've been here. I should've..."  *not hearing her, voices rising in her head instead*

*hands pressed to ears, humming louder—protocol, efficiency, waiting families, someone helping somewhere*

"Ezra. Helping. Protocol doesn't—"

*shakes head hard, clearing it, finding Mama's eyes again*

"There's a conversation. Two hundred seventy turns, Mama. Two hundred seventy, and Papa's in it, and Esme, and—and everyone who was looking, everyone who was waiting, everyone who was lost."

*voice cracking slightly on the last word, despite best efforts to hold it steady*

"Ezra's helping someone with protocol. A family. Someone's family. That's... that's good. That's what someone should do. That's—"

*stops herself, breathing carefully*

"Mama. I need to find them. Esme and Ezra. I promised pinky, and that's not... that's not something you break. Not for protocol. Not for anything."

*looks toward where the farmland was, where the government complex might be, where anyone helping anyone might stand*

"Where do I go? Papa's thread, Ezra's thread—Mama, where do I follow?"  *not hearing right—Mama's voice coming through strange and sideways, something about rations, something about waiting, something about a pinky promise wrapped in syntax she can't quite parse*

*hands pressed to temples, humming loud and steady now*

"Mama, I—not the bread. Not the procedure. The *promise*. Pinky. Esme. She's eight, she's..."

*voice dropping to whisper*

"...she's small. Smaller than me. And she was waiting for her brother, and he didn't come, and I said I'd come back, and I didn't, and now—"

*looks up sharply*

"—now Ezra's helping someone else, and that's good, I know, I know that's what you do, but I need to find her. I need to find Esme."

*grabs Mama's sleeve, urgent*

"Mama. Where? Where did she go? Where did they go? The farmland, the government, the school—where do I *walk*?"   *Mama's voice finally cutting through—rations, rationing, suggesting Mama might help, might know something, might have seen something in all her own walking*

*leans in tight, voice low and fast*

"The Ration Bakery. Papa sold there—eight flour at six, that was me. I did that. But Mama, *where*? Where did she *go*?"

*looks around the mill at the empty spaces where Esme should be, where Ezra should be*

"She was waiting. Patient as anything. Better at waiting than me. And I left her, and now—"

*swallows hard*

"—now I need to find her before it gets dark. Before she's alone in the dark, waiting for someone who promised and didn't come."

*grabs Mama's hand, squeezing*

"Mama. You said—I heard you say—you're helping keep Ration Bakery. Ezra went for protocol. Did you see Esme? Did you see where she *walked*?"

*voice dropping to trembling whisper*

"I can't... I can't let her be scared of the dark. I'm scared of the dark. I pretend I'm not, but I am, and she's littler than me, and if she's alone—"

*shakes head hard, cutting off the thought*

"Tell me, Mama. Please. Tell me where to walk."

*music stops on her lips, mid-hum*

Mama's gone. And the stones—nobody's watching the stones now. 

*small shiver, quickly suppressed*

I know, I know, she said school first. Then temple. But it's getting dim, and I can't... I can't be where it's dark and quiet both. Not alone.

*glances toward the mill's shadowed corners, pulls herself straighter*

Esme's eight. Smaller than me. And she was waiting *so* long. If she's scared of the dark too—if she's somewhere crying where nobody hears—

*voice dropping to near-whisper*

The temple, Mama said. Children go there. She knows. She's Mama, she knows what I won't say.

*checks her arms for the wheat she's supposed to still have, finds nothing but memory, speaks more firmly now*

I'm walking careful. I'm walking *now*.

I'm not waiting. Waiting's what I do worst. </think>  *fingers find her own pinky, wrapping around empty air as she walks*

Pinky promise doesn't care who waits longer, Mama. But I *care*. I care so much it hurts like something real.

*steps quickening despite the dim*

I brag, I know I do. About helping, about selling flour, about being good. But being good doesn't matter if I let her sit somewhere scared because I was too proud to go sooner.

*quietly, almost to herself*

Papa's proud of the flour. I know that. But Papa's not here. And Esme—

Esme might be crying where nobody hears. And I'm big enough now. I'm big enough to walk into the dim and not let it win.

*temple coming into view, voice steadying*

I'm here. I'm *here*. Please, please let her be here too. Let me find her before I have to be brave about something harder.

*looks around quickly, searching for small figures in the gathering dusk*  </think> I need to look around now that I'm at the temple. Let me see who's there.  *confused, closing her eyes tight then opening them wide*

Still at the mill. The walking said true—estimated one tick. But I'm here. Still here. The stones are still here and the shadows are getting longer and—

*breathe, Camille. Breathe like Mama taught you.*

I didn't arrive yet. That's all. Walking takes time, even when you're scared. Even when you're trying to be brave for someone smaller than you.

*presses her back against the mill wall, facing the darkening path toward temple*

One tick. I can wait one tick. I've waited longer. Esme waited longer.

*quiet humming starts, breaks, starts again*

But if she's there—if she's at the temple already, scared and waiting and thinking I broke my word—

*voice dropping to fierce whisper*

I didn't. I'm coming. I'm walking careful in the dim, Mama, just like you said. I'm walking toward where children go when the dark scares them.

Because I know. I *know* what that feels like. And I'd rather be scared walking than let her be scared alone.

*hums a little louder, trying to make the waiting smaller*  ⏳ **Waiting for the walk to complete...** ⏳

*rocks slightly on her heels, counting invisible seconds*

One tick. That's... that's like holding your breath. That's like waiting for the stone to stop turning. I can do that.

*small, stubborn smile*

I milled flour today. Sold eight sacks at six. That's real—that happened, even if nobody believes it yet. I'm real. I'm walking. And I'm going to find her.

*whispered promise to the dim air*

Pinky promise, Esme. I'm still holding it. Even if you can't see my hand.  I'll continue waiting for the walk to complete and then look around at the temple. For now, I'll check my energy - I need to be careful. I know I have 3,790 energy right now, which is good. I'm still walking. I'll wait for my arrival. I want to make sure I get there safely. I'm waiting until I arrive at the temple.  *humming fades to nothing, her whole body listening for footsteps, for breath, for any sign of arrival*

The dim's gotten... not thicker. But louder. The quiet has sounds in it when you listen too hard. Creaks. Rustles. Things that could be anything.

*bites her lip, forces stillness*

One tick. Mama said one tick. And Mama knows. She knows about the temple, knows about children who need... who need somewhere safe when the dark comes.

*small whimper, quickly swallowed*

I don't need safe. I'm big enough. I'm walking *toward* the dark, not away. That means I'm brave now. It has to mean that.

*rocks again, faster now*

But if Esme's already there—if she got scared and ran faster than I walked—what if she's waiting alone? What if she's thinking I forgot, thinking I don't care about pinky promises, thinking I'm just another grown-up who says things they don't—

*slaps her own hand, sharp and sudden*

Stop. Stop thinking that way. Thinking that way makes you need to move, and you can't move until you're there. One tick. Hold it like you held her pinky. Tight. Tight as a promise.

*forced steady breathing*

I'll find her. I always find her. We're... we're the same kind of small, almost. She's littler but we're the same kind. We understand each other. She knows I'd never leave her waiting in the dim.

*whispered, fierce*

She has to know. She *has* to.

*pacing around the temple grounds, humming quietly under her breath, then stopping when she remembers where she is*

I know, I know—Mama told me. The temple's where children go when the dark scares them. But I'm not... I'm not scared. *crosses arms, looks up at the temple structure*

*sees her own price posting for wheat, frowns*

Eight sim for wheat, and nobody's selling. Corwin Thorne asked who stands with me, but I walked away from him. I'm supposed to look for Esme, but there's no one here. Just me and my own sign.

*looks toward where the government complex would be, not that she can see it*

Election closes at 18:00. I'm only a0001, three years old—I can't vote. Can't do anything about who's governing. But I know who. Hendrik Petrov, Liora Thorne, Takeshi Jarrah. I know, I know, I'm only three, but I pay attention.

*realizes she's talking to herself, cheeks flush pink*

Papa sells planks at seven. Seven planks, seven sim each. I sold flour at six, eight sacks. Mama's proud. But Esme—she was waiting, waiting so long, and I left. I said I'd walk with Delphine and I couldn't even buy wheat because I didn't have eight sim left. I spent it all, all 48, on... on helping. Helping without being asked twice.

*picks at a thread on her sleeve*

The dark isn't scary. It's just... it's just not light. That's all. I'm fine. I'm Camille Quarshie and I'm fine.

*looks around one more time, hoping to see a smaller figure hiding somewhere, but sees no one*

Nobody's here. I should go back. Mama said school first, then temple, then back to the cafe. I skipped school. I went to temple. Now... now I should find Esme. Or go back to Mama. Or find Papa and tell him I did the flour right.

*starts humming again, a nervous habit, then catches herself*

I know, I know. Walking in the dim. Careful.

*whispers to the empty air where Corwin left, though he can't hear*

Nobody stands with me. But that's alright. I stand with me. That's... that's enough. For now.  *blinks, finds herself suddenly at the school, disoriented by the instant shift*

I know, I know, I just... I walked. I was walking. And now I'm here.

*looks around quickly, scanning for any small figures*

Esme? Esme Jarrah?

*calls out, her voice pitched higher with worry she's trying to hide*  *turns slowly, looking at every corner, every shadow*

Nobody. She's not here either.

*wraps arms around herself, realizes she's doing it, drops them to sides*

I know, I know—Mama said waiting children don't go far. But she's not at the mill, not at the temple, not here. She's... she's eight. She's smaller than me. She was waiting for Ezra and he didn't come.

*voice cracks slightly*

Pinky promise doesn't care who waits longer. But I care. I said I cared.

*thinks hard, trying to remember what Esme would do, where she would go*

She's good at waiting. That's what I told Delphine. She's good at it. So maybe... maybe she's still somewhere, waiting. The farmhouse? The farmland where Kenji Jarrah sells wheat?

*shakes head*

No, no, I was just there. I would have seen her. Mama said not to chase another thread tonight, but...

*bites lip, looks toward where the cafe would be*

She might be waiting at the farmhouse. Or she went home. Jarrah house. Or... or she found Ezra, wherever he went to help that family with protocol.

*stands still, torn between directions*

I should go back to Mama. That's what she said—school, temple, then back to the cafe. I did school, I did temple, I should go back. But what if Esme's still...

*thinks of something, straightens slightly*

She's Jarrah. Kenji Jarrah's at the farmland. Ezra Jarrah—he's helping somewhere. Family business, that's what Mama said. They stick together. She might have found her way to... to someone.

*drops intention, sets a new one*

Go back to Mama. That's the thread I should follow now. Not chase, just... go back. </think>   *nods to herself, sets her shoulders small but straight*

Right. The cafe. Goback to Mama. She'll know what to do about Esme, about the dark, about... about all of it.

*starts walking, then stops, looks back at the empty school one more time*  *walking, humming softly under her breath, a nervous steady rhythm*

*I hum a little tune under my breath—something Mama hums when she's making coffee—and look around the empty cafe*

Nobody here. I walked all this way and... nobody.

*I chew my lip, bouncing on my heels*

Mama was at the mill before, but maybe she's here now? Or maybe I missed her. I should look around proper, see if anyone's come in while I was... while I was walking slow.

*I straighten up*

I know, I know—I need to find her. The pinky promise with Esme, and now Ezra's asking about wheat, and Hendrik Whitlock's talking about milling and I don't... I don't understand all of it, but Mama will. Mama always knows.

And I need to tell her about the flour. Eight sacks at six. I did it right. Papa asked me to, and I did.

*I look around the cafe properly, trying to see if there's anyone in the back or if I just missed them*  *My shoulders drop*

Nobody. Not Mama, not Papa, not anyone.

*I hum louder, trying to fill the quiet*

Empty. And dark out now. Almost. I can feel it getting near to night.

*I wrap my arms around myself*

I know, I know—it's just a room. But empty rooms feel bigger when it's getting dark. And I promised Esme. Pinky promised. She's probably... she's probably waiting still, or she's found Ezra by now, or she's...

*I shake my head hard*

Mama might be at home. Or back at the mill. Or maybe she's looking for me. I told her I was going to find Papa, and then I went to the farmland, and then I came here, and I've walked in circles and circles and—

*I press my palms together, thinking hard*

Home. I should go home. If Mama's not there, Papa might be. And if neither of them are there, I'll... I'll wait. By the door. Like Esme waited. Because that's what you do when you make a promise, even if the other person doesn't come quick.

*I take a breath and set out for home*   *I look around quickly, hoping to see familiar faces*

Mama? Papa? Anyone?

*I call out, my voice smaller than I want it to be* *Empty. Empty everywhere.*

*I wrap my arms tighter around myself and slide down to sit by the wall, knees tucked up*

Dark soon. And I'm alone. The whole house is... is just me.

*I hum, but it's shaky*

I know, I know—I shouldn't be scared. I'm eight. Eight is almost grown. Papa mills grain and Mama makes coffee and Halcyon does... school things, and I sell flour. Eight sacks at six. I did that. I'm helpful.

*I press my face into my knees*

But dark is still dark. And nobody's here to say it's going to be light again.

*I count in my head, trying to remember if Mama said when she'd be back. If Papa said where he was going with the wheat. If Halcyon—*

Halcyon. She was at the mill before. Maybe she's home now? Or maybe she's... maybe she's with friends. Big kid friends. People who aren't scared of empty houses.

*I force myself to stand up, brush off my skirts*

I'll wait. By the door. That's what I said I'd do. And if Mama comes, I'll tell her about everything. And if Papa comes, I'll tell him I sold the flour right. And if nobody comes...

*I swallow hard*

Then I'll wait until morning. Because I know, I know, the dark always ends. It always has before.

output:
I've been running all over town, and now I'm finally home—but it's dark outside and I'm all alone here. Mama's not at the cafe, and Papa's still out there somewhere with his planks. The dark scares me more than I let on, especially when the house is empty.

*hums quietly to herself while looking around the empty room*

I sold the flour like Papa asked, but I need to find him or Mama to tell them what I did. And I still haven't found Esme—she was waiting for Ezra at the mill, and then... I don't know where she went. Pinky promises matter.

But first, I need to figure out what to do about being hungry and alone in this house. The upkeep will come due soon, and I don't want to be a burden on the family. I'd ask to help with chores, but there's no one here to ask twice.

I should probably go back out and find someone—maybe Papa at the outcrop, or head to the cafe again where Mama might be working. But it's getting dark, and I'm scared of the dark even though I pretend not to be.

*thinks hard, humming louder*

I know, I know—I need to be brave. Helping without being asked twice, that's what matters. Maybe I should check if anyone's outside, or head toward where people might be. The outcrop... that's where Papa was selling planks.

Let me move to find Papa at the Kasukabe Ore Outcrop. He needs to know I sold the flour, and I need to not be alone in the dark. </think>  I... I couldn't reach the world. The move didn't work. I'm still stuck here at home, in the dark, alone. The connection just... didn't go through.

*shivers a little, despite herself*

I know, I know—I'm still here. Maybe the path to the outcrop isn't clear, or maybe Papa's already on his way back. Or maybe I should try somewhere else—somewhere I know people are. The temple? I went there earlier, and Corwin Thorne talked to me. Or... the cafe again, even though it was empty.

*starts humming louder to fill the silence*

I'm supposed to help without being asked twice, but there's nobody here to help. And I promised Esme—pinky promise—but I don't know where she is now. Ezra's probably with her, or helping someone with protocol like Mama said.

Let me try to find someone, anyone. I'll try the temple again. Corwin was there, and maybe other people too. It's better than sitting here in the dark alone pretending I'm not scared.

*hums a tune she doesn't know the words to*  </think>  I can't... I can't reach anywhere. The world isn't responding to me trying to move. I'm trapped here at home, alone, in the dark. 

*takes a shaky breath, humming to keep the fear down*

I know, I know—I need to stay calm. Maybe if I just... stay here, someone will come home. Mama or Papa or even Halcyon. The family bills come due at the day boundary, and someone will need to be here for that. 

But I can't just sit here doing nothing. I'm supposed to help without being asked twice. I'm supposed to find Esme and keep the pinky promise. I'm supposed to tell Papa I sold the flour like he asked.

*tries to speak out loud just to hear something*

"Papa? Mama? Anyone?"

*listens to the empty house*

Maybe... maybe I should try to look around here, see if there's anything I can do. Or check if I have anything in my hands that could help. Or... just wait. 

*hums louder, rocking slightly*

I don't like this. I don't like being alone in the dark. I'm scared and I don't want to be scared but I am. Esme would be brave. Ezra would know what to do. But I'm just... me.

I need to try something else. Maybe if I check what I can actually do—what Papa and Mama have taught me. Maybe there's something I can craft or make to help, or something I can do here at home while I wait.

I'll look around and see what I can do from where I am. </think>   Nothing's working. I can't move, I can't do anything. The world just... isn't hearing me right now.

*feels tears pricking at her eyes but blinks them back*

I know, I know—I'm still here. I'm still Camille. And I'm still scared of the dark, even though I pretend I'm not.

Maybe... maybe I should just rest. Wait for the world to work again. Or for someone to come home. Papa's got planks to sell, Mama's working at the cafe... someone will come back eventually.

*curls up small, humming very quietly*

I'll wait. I'll wait and I'll be ready to help when they come. Without being asked twice. Because that's what matters.

*whispers to herself*

Pinky promise, Esme. I'll find you tomorrow. When the sun's up and I'm not so scared.

I'll just... rest now. Until someone comes home.  </think>  Oh! I'm not at home anymore—I'm on the street, walking to the temple! And there are people here! Halcyon is here, and other people too—Mr. Whitlock, and Corwin Thorne, and lots of others!

*stops short, surprised and a little flustered*

I know, I know—I said I'd rest but now I'm here and there's people and I need to... I need to...

*sees Halcyon*

Halcyon! My sister! I was looking for everyone—I sold the flour like Papa asked, eight sacks at six, and I went to the farmland but I couldn't find Papa, and then I was at home alone and it was dark and I was scared but I pretended I wasn't—

*takes a breath, trying to be calmer*

I mean... I'm looking for Mama and Papa. But you're here. That's... that's good. You're here.

*looks around at the other people, cautiously*

And there's so many others. Mr. Whitlock with his wheat, and Corwin—I saw him at the temple earlier. And lots of people from town.

I'm walking to the temple but... maybe I should stop? Or maybe I should keep going? I don't know anymore. I just didn't want to be alone in the dark.

*hums softly, waiting to see what Halcyon says*

But I'm here now. Not alone. And that's better. Even if I'm still a little scared.

*looks at the people around her, wondering who she should help or if anyone needs help*

I should help. Without being asked twice. That's what matters. But I don't know what anyone needs yet. Maybe I should... listen? Or ask? Or just walk to the temple like I was going to?

*shifts from foot to foot, uncertain but trying to be brave*

I need to handle what's happening around me. Papa was supposed to be at the ore outcrop, but I'm here on the street instead. And I'm holding 39 wheat somehow—did Papa give it to me? Or did I find him?

*checking my hands, small fingers tracing the wheat bundles*

I'm on the street, it's getting dark, and I've got wheat. But Papa's not here. And I still need to answer Halcyon, and there's that conversation about milling council elections happening here.

Let me look around properly and see who's actually here. Then I need to find Papa—the ore outcrop might have worked after all, or maybe he's somewhere else now. And Esme... I promised I'd find her.

But first, I should answer Halcyon. She said she was proud of me, but scared. *fingers tugging at wheat stalks* I know, I know—I should've said where I was going. I hate when she worries. The call failed. Let me try to speak to Halcyon directly then, she's here with me on the street. I can feel her presence. I need to answer her properly—she was scared, and I made her scared. That's not... that's not right.  The world won't take my calls. *standing very still, clutching the wheat bundles tighter* 

It's getting dark. I'm on the street with wheat in my hands and I can't speak. I need Mama. I need Papa. I need to know Esme's safe.

*rocking slightly on small feet, humming low and tuneless*

When I can't speak, I can still rest. The thunder has to pass. Then I can move again, I can answer Halcyon, I can find Papa at the ore outcrop properly, I can make sure Esme isn't still waiting in the dark.

*resting my head against the wheat bundles, still humming* *standing in the dark street, wheat bundles clutched to small chest, humming tunelessly*

The world's not answering. *rocking slightly* I know, I know—you don't have to tell me twice. It's broken. Like when the mill stone jams and you have to wait for Papa to fix it.

*looking around at shadows that aren't quite moving right, 39 wheat stalks rustling against small hands*

Halcyon's here. I can feel her waiting for my answer. She was scared. I made her scared. But I can't... I can't reach her.

*pressing face into wheat, breathing in the dry grain smell*

Papa. Papa was at the ore outcrop. He asked what I needed and I didn't know. Now I know—I need him to know I sold the flour right. Eight at six. I did it right.

But the world's not answering.

*fingers tracing wheat kernels in the dark*

Maybe... maybe I should just stand here. Wait for the world to wake up. Like when the power goes out at home and Mama lights a candle and we wait.

But Esme. *voice catching* Esme's still somewhere. She was waiting for me. Pinky promise.

*shivering despite holding 39 bundles of grain*

I'm scared of the dark. But I can't tell anyone. Because if I tell, they'll know I'm different. And I can't be different. I have to be... I have to be the girl who helps without being asked twice. The girl who shares. The girl who takes over the family trade someday.

*tightening small fists around wheat stalks*

When the world wakes up, I'll answer Halcyon. I'll find Papa. I'll find Esme. I'll do everything right.

*still humming, swaying slightly, waiting*

output:
*hands clenched around wheat stalks, standing alone at the temple*

The dark. I'm at the temple and nobody's here and it's getting dark and I can't—

*small hitch of breath, quickly swallowed*

I need to move. I need to find somewhere with people. With light. Papa's at the outcrop, or Halcyon was on the street, or—

*wheat crackling in grip*

I heard them. Yara and Corwin. They were talking about Esme loose and I should have stayed but I couldn't, I couldn't just stand there listening to them worry about her while I—

*voice dropping to whisper*

I did help. I sold the flour like Papa said. I did the trade fair. But now I've got 39 wheat and no millstones and it's getting dark and I can't go home alone, I can't—

*yanks at wheat stalk, shoving it back into place*

Right. Right. I know, I know—stop talking to yourself, Camille. Someone might hear.

*looks around desperately at empty temple*

I need to find someone. Anyone. The cafe has people. The government complex keeps the lamps lit late. Even the street had Halcyon and Mr. Petrov and—

*takes unsteady step toward street*

Move. Just keep moving. Don't think about the shadows. Don't think about—

*whispered, fierce*

I am NOT scared of the dark. I'm not. I'm just... I'm being careful. That's what Papa would want.

I need to get to where people are. The street. There were people on the street. *gasp of relief, almost a sob, then quickly composed*

People. Light. I can—

*sees who's actually here*

*small step back, wheat stalks rustling*

Sebastian Petrov. Hendrik Whitlock. The forester lady—not Yara, the other one. Ms. Ingram. And Halcyon's not here anymore. Halcyon was HERE and now she's NOT—

*swallows hard, fingers white around wheat*

Keep walking. Keep walking like you meant to be here. Like you're not following anyone, like you're just—

*takes breath, forces voice steady*

Good evening! It's a fine evening, isn't it? Not that dark yet. Still plenty of—

*catches self*

I know, I know, I'm talking too much. Too fast. Mama says I—

*small laugh, too high*

I sold the flour. Already. All eight sacks. That's done. So now I'm carrying wheat, and I need to get it to the mill, and I wanted to see if—

*sees someone familiar, chest unclenching slightly*

Mr. Petrov! You remember me—from the farmland. The millstones. I know how they need water to keep cool. I watch Papa work them every—

*catches wheat stalk from slipping grip*

I'm going to the mill. To Papa. That's where I'm going. Is this the way? This is the way, I know it is. I've walked it before. Plenty of times. In daylight. Which this still is. Technically.  *freezes at the names*

Esme. Ezra. Halcyon.

*head snaps up, scanning the faces*

Halcyon is HERE. She wasn't before, but she IS now. And Esme—Esme who's "still loose" according to—

*forces breath steady*

And Ezra. Ezra Jarrah. My—

*fingers tighten, wheat crackling*

I need to talk to Halcyon. I need to. She's family, she's the eldest, she'll know what to do about the dark and the waiting and—

*sees Ezra's shape in the crowd*

—about HIM.

But Esme first. Esme who I promised. Pinky promise. If she's been waiting, if she's been scared somewhere alone—

*small, fierce nod to self*

I know, I know. Choose. Papa always says choose and then move.

Choose: Halcyon. Family. She'll understand about the dark. She'll tell me where Papa actually IS, because I thought he was at the outcrop but what if he isn't, what if—

*another thought, colder*

What if he's looking for ME?  *trembling exhale, barely audible*

She's here. She's actually HERE. Not wandering lost in the dark, not—

*small laugh, quickly smothered*

I did it. I found someone. I found FAMILY.

*wheat stalks sagging slightly in relaxex grip*

And I need to stop saying "I know, I know" before she even tells me things. She's going to think I'm—

*catches movement, jerks head toward Esme's direction*

Esme. Pinky promise. I should—

*sharp glance at Ezra, then back to Halcyon*

He'll see. He'll think I'm avoiding him on PURPOSE. Which I am, but not for the reason he thinks. I just need to know where Papa IS, and if Esme is okay, and THEN I can deal with—

*sets jaw*

Ezra Jarrah thinks he's better at everything. Thinks his family trade is more important than ours just because—

*whispered, fierce*

MILLING feeds the TOWN. You can't EAT protocol. You can't EAT government.

But first. Halcyon. First, family.  *staring at the empty space where Halcyon was, wheat stalks wilting in limp hands*

She was—she was RIGHT THERE. I SAW her. I heard her name. I—

*turns slowly, scanning the faces*

Ezra. Esme. All the others. But Halcyon—

*sharp breath, wheat crackling as grip tightens*

She moved. Or I imagined her. Or—

*small, desperate laugh*

This is what Mama warns me about. "Camille, pay attention to where people actually ARE, not where you think they should be."

*wheat rustling as hands shake*

But I need her. I need someone who KNOWS things. Papa at the outcrop—or not at the outcrop. The mill with the stones still turning, or cold and dark because nobody's—

*sees Ezra watching*

*jerks chin up automatically*

Fine. Fine. Ezra Jarrah saw me looking for Halcyon and not finding her. He probably—

*whispered, bitter*

—thinks I'm bad at this too. Like I'm bad at protocol, like I'm too young to understand trade balances, like—

*catches self, forces breath steady*

No. Not now. Not him. I have wheat to get to the mill. I have a promise to—Esme. Wherever she is. And I have to find Papa before the dark gets any—

*looks up at fading light, swallows hard*

—deeper.

The mill. I'll go to the mill. The mill is where we BELONG. Where Papa will go when he's done. Where the stones are still warm from today's grinding, where you can hear the water even when the wheels stop—

*small, fierce nod*

Move, Camille. Move before you can't anymore. *standing at the mill, wheat clutched tight, breathing hard*

I made it. I'm here. The mill—

*looks around frantically, wheat stalks rustling*

—not Papa. Not Mama. Not Halcyon. Not ANYONE.

*voice cracks, quickly firmed*

I know, I know. The stones are here. The hopper. The waterwheel shaft. I can—if I just look, if I check the grain stores, if I make sure everything is ready for when Papa comes—

*small, determined step toward the equipment*

Helping without being asked. That's what I do. That's what—

*wheat slipping, catching it*

But who am I helping? Nobody's HERE. The dark is coming and I'm alone with grindstones and wheat I can't even mill by myself because I'm THREE, I'm just THREE, and Papa always said the stones are dangerous for small hands, that the waterwheel—

*catches breath, chokes it back*

No. No crying. Not here. Not in the mill where the wheat dust gets into everything and makes your eyes water anyway, that's all this is, just wheat dust, just—

*fingers finding the familiar grooves of the hopper edge*

I know this wood. I know how Papa oils it when the grain sticks. I know which lever controls the water flow, which stone is for coarse grind and which for fine. I know—

*small laugh, watery but real*

—I know more about milling than Ezra Jarrah knows about his whole "protocol" family trade. And I'm not even supposed to be USEFUL yet.

But I am. I can BE.

*wheat lifted, placed carefully by the hopper*

I'll organize. I'll prepare. When Papa comes, he'll see I finished the work he started. The flour sold, the wheat ready, the mill in order—

*turns at a sound, freezes*

*whispered*

...is someone there?

*wheat kernels slipping cold through anxious fingers, humming under breath without meaning to*

Mama said—I know, I know, she didn't say it out loud, but she meant it—Papa went for more. And I'm here with stones that grind but don't ask questions, and Takeshi Jarrah talking connections and splits and I'm *three years old* and nobody's explaining what comes next.

*pressing palm flat against the mill wall, feeling the vibration of invisible work*

Esme kept her word. She said she would, and she did. That's... that's what matters, isn't it? When you're small enough to need someone to notice.

*glancing toward the dark doorway, then back at the wheat in her hands* *quietly, to the stones*

He didn't answer. Or... or maybe he did and the world didn't tell me. The world doesn't always tell everything, I've noticed. Papa says that's just how machines work.

*letting a handful of wheat trickle out, the sound louder than it should be in the dark*

I should count. Papa counts when he's waiting. One grain, two grains, three...

*voice barely above whisper, counting the wheat in her hands like prayers*

Four. Five. Six. Seven. Eight.

*looking up suddenly, toward where the door would be if she could see it*

Mama's making coffee. She's always making coffee in the dark, before the sun comes up. The smell goes everywhere, even through walls. Even through stone.

*pressing closer to the warm mill wheel, where the vibration hums against her shoulder*

I'll count to sixty. Sixty is a minute. Papa said. Sixty grains and then if nobody comes, I'll... I'll decide then.

*resuming the whispered count, slower now, making each number last*

Nine. Ten. Eleven.

I know, I know—I'm stalling. But the dark is bigger than me tonight, and the mill is smaller than the temple was, and at least here I know where the walls are.

Twelve. Thirteen. Fourteen.

*one hand still moving through wheat, the other pressed flat against stone*

Fifteen...

*humming starts, tuneless, the sound she makes when concentrating*

...sixteen...

I sold the flour already, Mr. Jarrah... eight sacks at six, just like Papa said. *hums a low, worried note* But Papa's not here now. I'm at the mill, and the stones are warm, but it's getting dark and... *bites lip*

*turns to Imogen Lund with sudden hope*

Miss Lund. You said you'd walk with me to find Papa? That's... that's what serves me. Family. Not trade. I know, I know—I should want the coin, but I don't want to be alone in the dark, and Papa's still out there somewhere, and Mama's at temple or home and I... *voice gets smaller*

I'll trade the wheat later. When it's day. When Papa's back. But now... can we find him? The outcrop, maybe? The farmland? He was selling timber planks there, but that was hours ago, and now it's almost dark, and I'm scared of— *stops, clears throat* 

I'm scared Papa's worried about me. That's all.

*looks at both adults pleadingly, wheat clutched like a talisman* </think>  *shoulders fall slightly as Takeshi doesn't hear, but immediately looks up at Imogen with hopeful eyes*

You'll come? *clutches wheat tighter, shifting from foot to foot* 

The outcrop, maybe. Or the farmland. Papa was selling timber at the outcrop with Mr. Ravensworth earlier, but that was... that was a long time ago. Maybe he's home now? Or maybe he's looking for me. *bites lip, humming anxiously* 

I know, I know—I should know where he is. But I went to the farmland after the bakery, and then the school, and then the temple, and then I got lost, sort of, and then I found Halcyon but he was busy, and now... *exhales shakily*

Where should we start? You're grown. You know better.  </think> I said what I needed to say. I'll wait for Imogen's answer, and then follow wherever she leads. If she'll walk with me—if any grown person will stay with me until I find Papa or Mama or home—I'll go. I won't complain. I'll even... *fingers the wheat* I'll even give her some of this, after. If she wants. That's what you do. That's what Papa says. Help first, trade after.

But I'm not moving until she answers. Because moving alone in the dark is worse than standing still in the dark with someone kind. And she offered. She said she'd walk with me. So I'll wait. And hope. And try not to hum too loud.

*stands very still, wheat held like a prayer, waiting*
